- [o] F47 — P1: Write each host failure to the application log as an error line. On 2026-10-05 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64), only page lines take the `error: ` form, and the hosts write failures without it, for example `exposure settled failed: surface tab-… is not mounted` (Wails 4, Tauri 8), `host presentSurfaces failed while advancing the layout queue: …` and `sidecar: writer shutdown failed: Socket is not connected (os error 57)`, so a window check does not see them, although a window check fails on every application error logged while it runs. Each host log site that states a failure is classified as an error, which takes the `error: <where>: <text>` form in both hosts with the same text, or as an observation whose wording states the expected state, with a test of the line form at each owning host and a contract case for the shared form. Progress on 2026-10-05: two of the three examples were page lines, not host lines: the workbench sent `exposure settled failed: …`, `exposure: …` and `host <phase> failed while advancing the layout queue: …` through `report` without `error: `; `connectExposure` and `revisitRegistrations` now take the page's `report`, and the layout queue failure takes `errorLine`. [Hosts](spec/hosts.md#application-log) states that a host error line has the page form `error: <where>: <text>`, written through `LogError` (Go), `log_error` (Rust) and `sp_log_error` (native library), and that a host line without `error: ` is an observation that states the expected state; contract case `log.error.line-form`. Classification of the host, native and page sites: errors — every failed native call, event emit, endpoint read, write, close and encode, start document and installed module read, image reply, response, recovery and presentation failure (`error: image present: …`), sidecar write, close, kill, wait, read, protocol failure and restart failure, WebKit child record and kill failure, performance trace, menu command, window title bar, window prepare and close, surface layout cancel, notification and modal failure, Wails framework errors (`ErrorHandler`), and the native capture, surface settle, webview input and surface background failures; a late result that carries a failure after its request ended is now written as an error, because no request reports it; fatal exits after the log is open (`quit request`, `dock menu`, `main webview identity`, `file drop`, `window reveal`) stay fatal and write the error line first. Observations, worded as the expected state: `exposure reply … of removed surface … arrived after its request ended`, `<result> arrived after its request ended` for a completion whose caller already returned (it was `had no pending receiver`), the stale image frame line, `native event … of closed surface … arrived after the surface closed` (Wails), the buffered sidecar replies and closes, `sidecar <name>: connection lost; restarted`, the discarded disconnected connection, the service output after the ready bound, `sidecar <name>: the connection closed before its writer shut down` for ENOTCONN only (the reader reports the lost connection; another shutdown error is an error), the WebKit child reap decisions, the WebKit baseline count, and the native capture trace lines. `exposure settled failed: surface … is not mounted` is an error: every core command waits in `drawn` (`packages/workbench/index.html`) for each slot that names a native surface, and a slot whose surface was disposed after the last draw makes the wait throw, so the command answers without its settled wait; the sequence that leaves such a slot is F50. Native defects fixed in the same change: `surface_layout.m` wrote a literal `\n` instead of a line end, which joined the next log line to it, and the Tauri document close and background paths returned without a line when `platform::current()` failed. Red: `TestLogErrorWritesAnErrorLineToTheApplicationLog` and `log_error_writes_an_error_line_to_the_application_log` did not compile against the unchanged hosts (`undefined: host.LogError`, `unresolved import soksak_host_tauriv2::application_log::log_error`), native `application_log_test` did not compile (`'application_log.h' file not found`), `TestPresentationOutcomeNamesTheCurrentFrameOfAFailure` and `presentation_outcome_names_the_current_frame_of_a_failure` failed with `image present on main thread error: …`, and the workbench tests `a failed settling wait of a core command and a refused registration are error lines` and the layout queue assertion in `native preparation cannot present before DOM drawing and presents each ticket once` failed with the lines without `error: `. Green on macOS 26.6.2 arm64: the same tests pass; `make go-repeat PACKAGE=./packages/host/wailsv3/tests COUNT=1`, `make rust-repeat PACKAGE=soksak-host-tauriv2 COUNT=1`, `make host-contract-check` (353 cases), `make hosts-check boundaries exposure-check docs-check`, the Rust clippy and format checks, and the affected native tests pass. Retry condition for acceptance: a window run whose check failures include host error lines. Accepted in the ninth full window run of 2026-10-05 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 24 to 52; 339 of 342 checks passed): `a presentation that fails while the terminal service is stopped` failed on Tauri because of the host error line `error: image presentation timeout: …`, so host errors now fail window checks; the difference from Wails, which writes no such line, is F56.
- [o] F48 — P1: Find why a Tauri `status.get host.windows` failed with `runtime error: failed to receive message from webview`. On 2026-10-05 (load average 49 to 98), `tauriv2: a newly split terminal presents its first native raster` failed after 10.6s with that error. `tauri::Error::FailedToReceiveMessage` comes from `rx.recv()` after `run_on_main_thread` (tauri 2.11.5 `src/lib.rs:1091`) or from tauri-runtime-wry (`src/lib.rs:202`, `2084`), which means the closure that should answer was dropped without sending, not that the answer was slow. Which main-thread task was dropped and why is not yet known. Cause, read on 2026-10-05 from the sources (tauri, tauri-runtime and tauri-runtime-wry 2.12.1 as `Cargo.lock` pins them; the versions above were wrong): the text is `tauri_runtime::Error::FailedToReceiveMessage` (tauri-runtime `src/lib.rs:151`) from the `getter!` macro (tauri-runtime-wry `src/lib.rs:196-202`) of `window.title()` or `window.is_focused()` in `windows::list` (`packages/host/tauriv2/src/windows.rs:198-251`). That list reads each window's `closing` flag on the endpoint thread and then queries the window in separate main-thread round trips; when the main thread processes the window's close in between, our close listener sets `closing` and `on_window_close` sets the window's `inner` to `None` (tauri-runtime-wry `src/lib.rs:4351-4387`), and `handle_user_message` drops the reply channel of a window without `inner` without answering (`src/lib.rs:3214-3233`, `3574-3576`). The failing request was the first `host.windows` read of `fresh()` (e2e/app.mjs:581) right after it closed the project window that the previous library check left open (F49). Correction: read the flag and query every window in one main-thread step, so no close can come between them; `send_user_message` handles a window message at once on the main thread (`src/lib.rs:263-273`). Implemented on 2026-10-05: `windows::list` passes every registered window to `list_entries` (`packages/host/tauriv2/src/windows.rs`), which builds all entries in one main-thread step through `exposure::app_on_main`; `windows_changed` and `sidecars_changed` read the list through the same function. A window getter called on the main thread is handled at once and does not wait (tauri-runtime-wry `send_user_message`, `src/lib.rs:263-273`); it cannot deadlock on the runtime's window store, because `handle_user_message` runs `Message::Task` without a borrow (`src/lib.rs:3182`) and releases its borrow of the store before it answers a window message (`src/lib.rs:3214-3226`). The other host statuses do not read the `closing` flag: `host.window` reads one window, and `host.screens`, `host.dock` and `host.menu` read the application. Wails needs no change: `hostBackend.Windows` (`packages/host/wailsv3/src/exposure.go`) reads the title from host state, and `WebviewWindow.IsFocused` (wails v3.0.0-beta.27 `pkg/application/webview_window.go:781-786`) reads the native window on the main thread, where `destroy` has already set it to nil after closing it (`webview_window_darwin.go:1889-1901`), so a close during the list yields `false`, not an error. Red (macOS 26, worktree with `list_entries` running the entries on the calling thread as before, load 238): the new contract case `exposure.windows.listed-in-one-main-thread-step`, test `a_close_during_the_list_does_not_fail_the_list` in `packages/host/tauriv2/tests/exposure_test.rs`, which queues a close on a test main thread at the moment the list reads the flag, failed with `left: Err("runtime error: failed to receive message from webview")`, `right: Ok([main, w2])`. Green: the same test passes, and `make rust-repeat PACKAGE=soksak-host-tauriv2 COUNT=1` passes every Tauri host test, including `a_closing_window_is_left_out_without_querying_it` and `a_failed_query_of_an_open_window_is_reported`; `make host-contract-check` passes 353 cases. An earlier run of that check failed the unchanged `persistent_transport_replaces_endpoint_left_by_a_dead_service` in the default configuration with `the service did not print its endpoint within 30s` at load 402 while it passed in the diagnostics configuration; `make rust-repeat TEST=persistent_transport_replaces_endpoint_left_by_a_dead_service COUNT=3` passed 3 of 3 at load 324, so the failure is classified as load. Defect outside this correction: `host.window` (`window_status`) and the commands that call `native_owner_on_main` read the native window handle in one main-thread step and use it in a later one, so a close between the steps can pass a closed window's pointer to native code; whether the window object is freed before `Destroyed` is not yet verified, and the finding needs its own item. Acceptance: a window run in which `fresh()` closes windows without this error. Accepted in the ninth full window run of 2026-10-05 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 24 to 52; 339 of 342 checks passed): no `failed to receive message` line and no failure of `fresh()`.
- [o] F49 — P1: Decide and implement what happens to an open project window when its project is removed from the library. `library names a missing project folder and removes the project` (e2e/library.test.mjs) opens the project in its own window, removes the project with `core.library.remove`, and its cleanup closes only projects still in `core.projects`, so the window of the removed project stays open and the next check closes it. [projects](spec/projects.md) says the removal deletes the record and its spaces like closing a project tab, but not what happens to a window that shows that project. Decided and implemented on 2026-10-05 ([projects](spec/projects.md#settings)): closing a window's last project tab releases the window and shows the library in the same OS window (`projects.close`, host `projectRelease`), so a removal does the same in the window that shows the project; the window stays open as a window without a project and is not closed. That window read the removal through `readProjects` and showed the library, but kept the surface modules of the removed project's tabs, so the host kept their terminal sessions, and it did not open its next project tab. `readProjects` now ends every removed project in each window: it disposes the surface modules of its tabs, ends their sidecar sessions, and the change notification opens the window's first remaining project. Red: `projects-switch.test.mjs` `a project removed from the registry by another window ends in the window that shows it as closing its tab does` failed on the unchanged module with `the window did not open its next project as closing the project tab does` (actual `undefined`, expected `prj-next`); Green: it passes with the workbench suite (282 tests). The library check now waits on `host.windows` until the project window shows no project, on `core.screen` for the library, and on `host.window` until the native surfaces of the removed project's terminals are gone, then closes the window it opened. Acceptance: that library window check on both hosts. Accepted in the ninth full window run of 2026-10-05 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 24 to 52; 339 of 342 checks passed): `the library names a missing project folder and removes the project` passed on both hosts.
- [o] F50 — P1: Find why the settled wait of a core command finds a slot whose native surface is not mounted. On 2026-10-05 the seventh full window run logged `exposure settled failed: surface tab-… is not mounted` four times on Wails and eight times on Tauri. `drawn` in `packages/workbench/index.html` waits for the current draw and then for the composition of every slot with `data-native-surface-id`; `waitSurfaceCompositionDeclared` throws when the slot names a surface that `disposeSurface` already removed, which happens when a tab close or a project switch disposes a surface after the last draw and before the next one. Whether a command can overlap such a removal, which makes the removed surface a declared state that the wait skips, or whether a slot outlives its surface in one command, which is a defect of the draw order, is decided from the run evidence with a workbench test that reproduces the sequence. Cause, read on 2026-10-05 from the logs of the seventh full run and the targeted run that followed (e2e-full7 and e2e-target1, macOS 26.6.2 arm64): each line is written just before the page reload of the next check's `fresh()`, and in the terminal checks the check before it ends with `closeTerminalTabs`, which runs `core.tab.close` for every terminal tab one after another (Wails lines 22662 and 22742 follow `a presentation that fails while the terminal service is stopped …` and `a terminal split from a terminal starts in the directory …`; Tauri lines 537, 538 and 541 and target1 lines 831 and 834 follow the same checks). Two defects let a settled wait read a slot list older than a disposal. First, the `core.tab.close` handler (`core-exposure.js`) called `closeTabById(tab)` without returning its promise, so the command ran its settled wait and answered while `closeTab` was still disposing the surface; `closeTab` disposes the surface first and only then removes the tab and schedules the layout without its slot, so the next `core.tab.close` of the check, or the next check, ran its wait while the disposed surface still had its slot. `closeTab` had become asynchronous for this wait, but the handler did not change. Second, `drawn` (`index.html`) awaited the `drawing` promise once; a layout that a newer layout replaces resolves `{status: "superseded"}` without a draw, so a wait that began before the next tab close scheduled its layout ended before the draw that removes the slot and read the slots of the earlier draw; `layout: <n> waiting layouts were replaced by newer layouts before presentation` precedes most of the lines. Correction: `core.tab.close` awaits `closeTabById`, and `drawn` waits through `wait()` of the layout queue, which waits for the newest layout and waits again while a newer one was scheduled, and fails with the failure of the newest layout; [exposure](spec/exposure.md#registration) states the rule. The other lines (Wails 21081 and 21629, Tauri 498, 507, 517, 743 and 744, target1 800, 808 and 1065) also stand before the reload of a `fresh()` and after a replaced layout, but the run had no performance trace, so the logs do not name their command; the corrected wait covers every removal that schedules a layout. A disposal that leaves a slot without a scheduled layout remains only inside `closeTab` between the end of `disposeSurface` and its `settle()`, which run in one microtask checkpoint, so a wait cannot read the slots between them unless the same task resolves the layout that the wait awaits. Red: `core.tab.close answers after the tab close and its draw` (`test/tab-close-settled.test.mjs`) recorded `['close tab-a', 'settled']` before the close finished, and `the wait for the drawn layout continues through a layout that a newer layout replaces` read `["tab-a","tab-b"]` instead of `[]`, and `the wait for the drawn layout fails with the failure of the newest layout` failed with the error of the replaced layout. Green: the same tests and `pnpm -F @soksak/workbench test` pass. Acceptance: a window run without `exposure settled failed: surface … is not mounted`. Accepted in the ninth full window run of 2026-10-05 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 24 to 52; 339 of 342 checks passed): neither application log has a `is not mounted` line.
- [o] F51 — P1: Use a native window handle only in the main-thread step that reads it. `host.window` (`window_status` in `packages/host/tauriv2/src/exposure.rs`) and the commands that call `native_owner_on_main` (`surfaces.rs` lines 212, 370, 547, 740; `exposure.rs` lines 1247, 1366, 1543, 1582, 1656) read the native window handle in one main-thread step and pass it to native code in a later one, so a close between the steps can pass the handle of a closed window to native code such as `sp_window_facts`. Measured on 2026-10-05 from the sources (tauri-runtime-wry 2.12.1 and tao at rev 1a047e2, as `Cargo.lock` pins them): when no listener prevents a close, `on_close_requested` calls `on_window_close` in the same main-thread pass, and `on_window_close` sets the window's `inner` to `None`, which drops the last `Arc` of the tao window. `UnownedWindow::drop` then sends `close` to the NSWindow at once (`close_async` runs inline on the main thread), `windowWillClose:` removes the delegate and queues `Destroyed`, and the drop releases the two strong references that tao holds (`UnownedWindow.ns_window` and the copy in the delegate state; the window has `releasedWhenClosed` off). The NSWindow is therefore closed, and freed unless another owner retains it, before `Destroyed` is delivered, so a handle read before the close names a closed and possibly freed object. Progress on 2026-10-05: every Tauri request that uses the native window reads it in the main-thread step that passes it to native code (`windows::use_owner` through `with_native_owner`): `host.window`, `host.window.fullscreen`, `host.window.move`, `host.hit`, `input.pointer` (activation, delivery and surface press), `input.key`, the surface press watch, and the title bar, begin, commit and cancel steps of the surface layout; the initial title bar reads the handle in its own main-thread task. A window whose close was accepted, or whose registration `Destroyed` removed, is closed at that step: native code does not receive it, the request fails with 1003 `window "<name>" does not exist`, a `host.window` change of it notifies nothing, and a layout cancel of it has nothing to cancel because `Destroyed` cancels its layout. The surface press of `input.pointer` ran AppKit hit testing on the endpoint thread; it now runs in the main-thread step. The Tauri unknown-window message now quotes the name as Wails does. Wails already read `NativeWindow()` in the step that uses it, where Wails' destroy has set it to nil, but passed that nil to native code; through `UseNativeWindow` it now answers the same 1003. Red: with the handle read and used in two steps, the new Rust case `a_close_after_the_handle_read_does_not_reach_native_code` failed with `left: Err(Failed("native code messaged the closed window 0x5157")) right: Ok("facts of 0x5157")`; the new Go case `TestACloseBeforeTheNativeStepDoesNotReachNativeCode`, with the nil passed to native code, failed with `a window closed before the step: <nil>`. Green: both pass under the new contract case `window-close.native-window.used-in-reading-step`; the Tauri and Wails host suites, `make host-contract-check` (359 cases), `hosts-check`, `boundaries`, `docs-check`, `parity-check`, `exposure-check` and `pnpm test` pass on macOS 26.6.2 arm64 at load average 50 to 100. Open: the window checks against rebuilt hosts. Accepted in the ninth full window run of 2026-10-05 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 24 to 52; 339 of 342 checks passed): every window close and reload check passed on both hosts.

The same file has operations that return without an error (`CloseSurface`, `SetSurfaceBounds`, `SurfaceFrame`), although [hosts](spec/hosts.md#windows-state) says that every operation outside directory identity returns `<operation> is not implemented on windows`. The Rust host is to be checked the same way; the `aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm` and `x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm` targets are installed. The Windows builds also fail outside the Windows files. Go `src/sidecars.go:824` sets `syscall.SysProcAttr.Setsid`, and Rust `src/application_log.rs` uses `std::os::unix::fs` modes, so both are platform work in shared files and move into platform operations under `platform/<os>/`. The Go `Platform` rule that functions without an error take only handles from error-returning constructors is broken by `ConfigureMainWindow`, `PreferredLanguage`, `MainWindow` and `ServiceProcessExists`, which return errors in Rust and are to return them in Go. `cargo check --target aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm` needs a Windows C compiler (`aarch64-w64-mingw32-clang`) for `ring`. Every operation of `platform/windows/unsupported.*` returns `<operation> is not implemented on windows` or, without an error result in Go, panics with that error through `unreachable`; the Go `missing` and `unreachableError` helpers that did not exist are removed, and the operation names of both hosts are the same. Starting a process in a new session is the platform operation `NewSession` (Go) that Darwin implements with `Setsid` and Windows refuses. The Rust log files are created through `create_private_directories` and the new `append_private_file`, so `application_log.rs` uses no `std::os::unix`. `ConfigureMainWindow`, `PreferredLanguage`, `MainWindow` and `ServiceProcessExists` return errors in Go, and their callers report them: a failed theme answers the page with the error, a failed main window configuration ends the application through `fatalError`, and a menu command without the main window logs the error. The Rust initial menu language took the default language when the system language could not be read (`unwrap_or_default`); in both hosts that failure now fails startup. With errors from `ServiceProcessExists`, the Go host stopped treating a refused signal check (EPERM) as an existing process, and Rust already failed on it; both hosts now treat EPERM as an existing process, because the refusal shows that the process exists (contract case `sidecars-transport.endpoint.foreign-service-process-exists`). Red: on main, `make windows-build-check` failed with `unsupported.go:218:14: undefined: missing` and `unsupported.go:374:13: undefined: unreachableError`, and after the Windows-file fixes with `sidecars.go:824:42: unknown field Setsid`; `scripts/test/windows-build-check.test.mjs` failed on the unchanged Go host with the same errors; the new foreign-process cases failed with `cannot inspect service process 1: operation not permitted` (Go, after the signature change) and `Operation not permitted (os error 1)` (Rust). Green: the same test and cases pass; the Wails and Tauri host suites pass on macOS 26.6.2 arm64. For diagnosis only, `cargo check -p soksak-host-tauriv2 --target aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm` with zig as the C compiler (`CRATE_CC_NO_DEFAULTS=1`) failed on the unchanged `application_log.rs` with `cannot find unix in os` and passes after the change in the default and `diagnostics` builds; this is not evidence of the check. Open: `make windows-build-check-rust` fails with `FAIL: windows-build-check-rust requires the Windows C compiler aarch64-w64-mingw32-clang, which is not installed` until that compiler is installed; it then runs in `make hosts-check`. Completed on 2026-10-05: llvm-mingw 20260922 (clang 23.1.2, sha256 `52e5f5a7b131021d0c39a37a38fa380a1da7885cd04bd61afd0cd4ecfb8bc1f3`) is installed in `~/.local/opt/llvm-mingw`, the Makefile declares it as `LLVM_MINGW` and passes its compiler and archiver to `cc` through `CC_aarch64_pc_windows_gnullvm` and `AR_aarch64_pc_windows_gnullvm`, and `make hosts-check` runs `windows-build-check-rust`. Red: `hosts-check runs the Windows build check` failed without the Rust `cargo check` lines; Green: the three tests of `scripts/test/windows-build-check.test.mjs` pass, and both Rust checks (default and diagnostics) pass for `aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm`.

An image presentation timeout writes `error: image presentation timeout: pending surface=…` on Tauri and no host line on Wails, while both hosts and the page write `host presentSurfaces failed …`, `exposure settled failed …` and `page: surface presentation failed …` for the same failure, so `a presentation that fails while the terminal service is stopped` failed only on Tauri. The requester that receives a failure reports it, and a host writes an error line only for a failure that no request reports; that rule decides which of these lines remain. Progress on 2026-10-05: the three lines that both hosts were said to write are page lines: `host presentSurfaces failed while advancing the layout queue: …` from the continuation of the layout transaction order in `packages/workbench/host.js`, `page: surface presentation failed: …` from the layout queue's `failed` in `packages/workbench/index.html`, and `exposure settled failed: …` from the settled wait of the core command. [Hosts](spec/hosts.md#application-log) and [exposure](spec/exposure.md#registration) state the application of the rule, contract case `images.wait.timeout-writes-no-log-line`, and `a presentation that fails while the terminal service is stopped` declares only `/^error: page: surface presentation failed: the current image raster did not present within /`. The Rust host creates its private log file and directories through platform operations that return `not implemented on windows`, while the Go host's `OpenLog` and the `os.Chmod` in `sidecars.go` use portable `os` permission modes that compile on Windows without giving owner-only access. Resolved on 2026-10-05: both hosts create owner-only files and directories only through the platform operations `CreatePrivateDirectories`, `AppendPrivateFile`, `CreatePrivateFile`, `WritePrivateFile`, `SecureServiceDirectory` and `PrivateDirectory` in Go and `create_private_directories`, `append_private_file`, `create_private_file`, `write_private_file`, `secure_service_directory` and the diagnostic `private_directory` in Rust, which `platform/darwin/private_files.*` implements with modes 0700 and 0600; `CreatePrivateFile` and `create_private_file` are new and create a file that must not exist; `WritePrivateFile` and `write_private_file` are new and replace the contents of a file. Windows returns `private directory creation`, `private file creation`, `new private file creation`, `private file writing`, `persistent sidecar service directory` and `private directory` with `is not implemented on windows` in both hosts. The Go sites that now use them are the application and service logs, the configuration and settings directories, the process lock, the clipboard image and its directory, the service directory, the performance switch, service flags, output and logs directory, the WebKit child record, and the diagnostic recording, still-capture and fixture directories. The Rust host created the process lock (0644), the services, clipboard, settings, endpoint record and performance logs directories, the performance switch, service flags and output, the WebKit child record and the diagnostic fixture settings with the umask mode; it now uses the same operations, so these have the Go modes 0700 and 0600. Files of the temporary-file helpers (Go `os.CreateTemp`, Rust `tempfile`) keep the mode 0600 that the helpers set. [Hosts](spec/hosts.md#platform-interface) lists the operations. Red: the new Go cases failed to compile with `Platform has no field or method CreatePrivateDirectories` (and `AppendPrivateFile`, `CreatePrivateFile`), the new Rust cases with `no method named create_private_file`, and the Rust case `the_process_lock_is_owner_only` failed with `left: 420, right: 384` (mode 0644, want 0600); the Go process lock already had mode 0600. The new Rust cases `enable_creates_owner_only_files` and `the_webkit_child_record_is_owner_only` failed with `…/performance has mode 644` and `record has mode 644`. Green: the contract cases `platform.private.creates-owner-only-directories`, `platform.private.appends-owner-only-file`, `platform.private.creates-new-owner-only-file`, `platform.private.writes-owner-only-file`, `performance.trace.owner-only-files`, `webkit-children.record.owner-only` and `endpoint.process.lock-mode-0600` pass in both hosts on macOS 26.6.2 arm64, and `make windows-build-check` compiles the Go Windows implementation in the default and diagnostics builds. The Windows errors are checked only by that compilation, because the host tests run only on macOS. Accepted in the eleventh full window run of 2026-10-05 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 26 to 47; 339 of 344 checks passed): every check passed on both hosts with the owner-only files.
- [o] F60 — P1: Find why Tauri presents an image for a surface it does not find. In the tenth full window run of 2026-10-05, `both hosts answer the same page the same way` failed with the Tauri host line `error: image present: surface=tab-wlo6p3 name=view generation=256 raster=5 sequence=4 token=1451 reason=notFound current none`, which F47 made visible; Wails wrote no such line. Progress on 2026-10-05: `notFound` names the transfer image, not the surface: the native presentation (`sp_region_present` in `native/darwin/src/image_region.m`) found no IOSurface for the frame's token. Both hosts handle the case with the same code (`HandleEnvelope` in `packages/host/wailsv3/src/images.go`, `handle_envelope_with_recovery` in `packages/host/tauriv2/src/images.rs`) under the existing contract cases `images.present.failure-line-names-the-current-frame` and `images.present.rejects-frame-detached-during-main-thread`; Wails did not meet the timing in this run. The main-thread step checks the frame against the region state before it presents, so the region was attached when the IOSurface was missing, and `current none` shows that its state was removed right after that step. The check had started with `fresh` (`e2e/app.mjs`), which resizes the window, which configures a new raster, and runs `diagnostics.fixture`, which closes the previous check's project and disposes the module of its terminal tab `tab-wlo6p3`; that tab appears in no other line of the Tauri log. The terminal module's `dispose` sends the sidecar `close`, which ends the session and releases its transfer images, and then disposes its composition, which detaches the region; the shell module does the same. A frame that the supplier sent before `close` therefore reached a region that was still attached with a released transfer image. The error line is correct, and the cause is the order: the workbench now detaches the regions of a module's compositions before it calls the module's `dispose` (`disposeModule` in `packages/workbench/surface-modules.js`, [plugins](spec/plugins.md#surface-ownership)), so such a frame is answered `stale` for a detached region. No host change is needed, so the hosts have no Red test. Red: `removing a surface detaches its regions before the module ends its sidecar session` (`packages/workbench/test/surface-dispose-order.test.mjs`) failed with the order `["session close", "imageDetach view"]` against the expected `["imageDetach view", "session close"]`; Green: it passes, and the 297 workbench tests pass. Acceptance: a full window run whose application logs have no `reason=notFound` line. Accepted in the eleventh full window run of 2026-10-05 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 26 to 47; 339 of 344 checks passed): neither application log has a `reason=notFound` line.
- [o] F61 — P1: Find why a Tauri terminal close answered before its PTY child was reaped. In the tenth full window run of 2026-10-05, `closing terminal tabs reaps every PTY child without killing the shared service` failed on Tauri with `normal terminal close must reap every PTY child before the close answer` and child 12783 still present; the same check passed in the earlier runs. Cause, identified on 2026-10-05: the terminal service answers `closed` before its surface actor closes the session. The check waits until `host.sidecars` no longer lists the closed surfaces; both hosts remove a surface from that list only on the service's `closed` answer or on the loss of the connection (`close_answer` and `forget_closing` in `packages/host/tauriv2/src/sidecars.rs`, `closeAnswered` and `forgetClosing` in `packages/host/wailsv3/src/sidecars.go`), so core keeps the order that [sidecar messages](spec/sidecars.md#messages) require and the two hosts relay the answer the same way. In the service (sidecars/vt), `PersistentRegistry::close_surface` in `vt-core/src/protocol.rs` sends `SurfaceCommand::SessionClose` into the surface actor's queue, starts a task that awaits the actor, and returns `Ok`; the connection loop then writes `{surface, closed: true}` at once. The actor closes the PTY session (`PtyService::close` in `vt-core/src/pty.rs`, which waits for the reaper thread's `wait`) only when it takes that command from its queue, so the answer can precede the reap; the order depends on the actor's work at that moment, which makes the failure intermittent and independent of the host. The run's logs agree: neither host log has a `sidecar … close <surface>: …` line, and both host logs have the same four `connection lost; restarted` lines, so the Tauri closes were answered without error and not cleared by a connection loss. The service log has no timestamps or close lines. Two further service orders have the same form: the connection without a registry sends `SessionClose` without awaiting the actor (`close_connection_surface`), and `PtyService::close` that takes the child lock before a new session's reaper thread does returns after `kill` without reaping. The correction belongs to the service repository; core is unchanged. The correction belongs to the terminal service repository as its item S20; F61 stays open until S20 is released and `closing terminal tabs reaps every PTY child without killing the shared service` passes on both hosts with that service. Accepted in the eleventh full window run of 2026-10-05 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 26 to 47; 339 of 344 checks passed) with S20, S21 and S22 of the terminal service: `closing terminal tabs reaps every PTY child without killing the shared service` passed on both hosts.
- [o] F62 — P1: Find why the Wails persistent transport harness waited for a connection event that never came. On 2026-10-05 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 45), `TestPersistentTransportHarnessEndpointAuthConcurrentReconnectAndCloseAck` failed at its 120s limit with `sidecars_transport_test.go:205: no connection event; the test stalled`, and passed in both configurations of `host-contract-check` of the same run, 3 of 3 alone and in the next full run. A stall is a missing event, not a slow one, so it is not load. Resolved on 2026-10-05: the stall was a test race, not a missing host event. The service fixture `serveHarnessConnections` closed the first two connections that it accepted, after their first echo, and assumed that these were the first connections of the two hosts. When the first host's revived connection reached the service before the second host's first connection, the fixture closed the revived connection and kept the second host's connection open, so the second host lost no connection and published no connection event; the failed log has one `connection lost; restarted` line instead of two. The host publishes a connection event for each lost connection in this order. The fixture now selects the connection to close by its request: it closes a connection after it echoes an `open` request, and a revived connection, which carries `reconnect`, stays open; it also records its first error under a mutex. The Tauri harness already closes a connection only on the host's own `drop` request and has no such interleaving, so it is unchanged. The test gained the subtest `second opens after the first reconnected`, which opens the second host only after the first host's connection event. Red with the unchanged fixture: `sidecars_transport_test.go:190: no connection event; the test stalled` at 120.01s. Green after the correction: the same test 3 of 3 and the Wails host test package 1 of 1, on macOS 26.6.2 arm64.
- [o] F63 — P2: Find why the command supervisor's cleanup failed with `kill EPERM` after forwarding SIGTERM. On 2026-10-05 `forwards CLI SIGTERM to command cancellation and cleanup` (`scripts/test/test-command.test.mjs`) failed, and passed 3 of 3 alone and in the next full run. Resolved on 2026-10-05: the failing result was `fail` with the error `kill EPERM` and the only cleanup observation `verify` EPERM, so the refused call was the cleanup's existence probe `kill(-pgid, 0)`, not a signal; the line `SIGKILL to process group …: kill EPERM` of the same log belongs to the earlier test that injects that refusal. In XNU `killpg1` (`bsd/kern/kern_sig.c`) finds the group, skips members in state `SZOMB` and answers EPERM for a POSIX `kill` that found no member; a process leaves its group only when its parent reaps it (`reap_child_locked` in `kern_exit.c`). The command's descendant handles SIGTERM, so a SIGKILL of the supervisor ended it (the forced kill 100 ms after the forwarded SIGTERM or the cleanup's); its parent, the command, had already exited on SIGTERM, so launchd reaps it, and the group held only that zombie until launchd did, which took longer than the 300 ms of probes on the loaded machine; a group of this user's processes has no member with other credentials. On macOS 26.6.2 a group whose only member is an unreaped zombie answers EPERM for signal 0 and SIGKILL and ESRCH after the reap. The supervisor now reads the group's members from the process table after a refused probe (`groupMembers` in `scripts/test-command.mjs`), records them in the `verify` observation, and counts the group as cleaned when no listed member runs; a running member keeps the EPERM failure. The tests judge a descendant as ended by its process state, because `kill(pid, 0)` succeeds for a zombie. [Examples](operations/examples.md) states the rule. Red: `counts a process group that holds only zombies as gone after a denied probe` failed with `'fail' !== 'pass'` and the error `kill EPERM`; Green: it, `reads the members of a group from the real process table after a denied probe` and the 20 supervisor tests pass, and the four affected tests pass 3 of 3 in `make node-repeat`.
- [o] F64 — P1: Find why the files sidecar exited with SIGPIPE while Wails stopped it. In the eleventh full window run of 2026-10-05, `the application log file holds the lines the page reports` failed on Wails with the host line `error: sidecar @soksak/sidecar-files: exited while stopping: signal: broken pipe`, which F47 made visible. Cause: when the host stopped its sidecars it removed their surfaces from the closing list, and a standard-input sidecar that answered such a close on its way out was taken as a protocol violation (`unexpected close answer`), so the host stopped reading and closed the pipe; the sidecar's next write got SIGPIPE, which the host wrote as `exited while stopping: signal: broken pipe`. In Tauri, `stop` also emptied the running list, so every message during the stop was an `unknown surface` violation, and a violation during the stop was dropped without a line. Fix (both hosts): the host keeps the surfaces and the removed closes of a stopping sidecar, accepts their answers and messages, reads the output to its end, writes a violation during the stop as `failed: <reason>` without a failure event, writes a nonzero or signalled end as `exited while stopping: exit status <code>` or `signal <number>` through the new platform operation `ExitStatus`/`exit_status`, and writes a forced kill as `did not end within the stop timeout and was killed`; [sidecars](spec/sidecars.md) states the stop. Red: Go `TestStopReadsOutputToItsEnd` logged `exited while stopping: signal: broken pipe` and the sidecar could not finish its writes, `TestStopReportsExitStatus` logged `signal: terminated`; Rust `stop_reads_output_to_its_end` (writes not finished) and `stop_reports_exit_status` (empty log) failed; Green: all pass and `make host-contract-check` passes 371 cases. Its acceptance is the next full window run without the line. Accepted in the thirteenth full window run of 2026-10-05 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 58 to 93; 334 of 344 checks passed): no `exited while stopping` line.
- [o] F65 — P1: Find why the card header control did not open a folded left sidebar on Wails. In the eleventh full window run of 2026-10-05, `the card header has a fold control for each sidebar the card shows` failed after 20s with `the header control did not open the folded left sidebar again`; `core.grid` still reported the left sidebar `collapsed` and `requestedCollapsed`. Progress on 2026-10-05: the click did not run the command. The host log records no command, but the stored choice shows it: `core.card.sidebar.toggle` stores the opposite of the shown state, so a second toggle would have stored `collapsed: false`, and `requestedCollapsed: true` means no second toggle ran; no space fold applies, because `autoCollapsed` is false. Every draw of the card header moved both fold controls: `drawSideToggles` in `packages/workbench/plane.js` inserted each control before the card tools unless it already stood directly before them, which holds for at most one control, so with the top and left sides shown each draw moved the top and the left control with `insertBefore`. `insertBefore` takes a node out of the document before it inserts it again, and WebKit clears the target of a press when its node leaves the document (`EventHandler::nodeWillBeRemoved` sets `m_clickNode` to null), so the release sends no `click`. The check presses and releases through two host requests, and the draw of the first fold runs at an animation frame after its native preparation (F43) while `core.grid` already reports the stored fold, so that draw could fall between the second press and its release; Tauri passed because its draw did not fall there. The control now moves only when its order is wrong: from the last shown control backwards, a control moves only when its next sibling is not the next control (the card tools for the last), and the rule is stated in [exposure](spec/exposure.md#user-interface). No host change is needed, so the hosts have no Red test. Red: `a draw keeps the pressed card header fold control in the document` (`packages/workbench/test/plane-side-toggles.test.mjs`) failed with the removed controls `["top", "left"]` against the expected `[]` for the held draw of a left fold; Green: it passes, and the 301 workbench tests pass. Acceptance: a full window run in which the check passes on both hosts. Accepted on 2026-10-05 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, load average 15): `the card header has a fold control for each sidebar the card shows` passed 3 of 3 runs on both hosts.

- [o] F68 — P1: Write the WebKit child record without losing a write when page loads overlap. In the twelfth full window run of 2026-10-05 and its rerun of the failed files, Wails logged `error: webkit children record: rename: rename …/webkit-children.json.new …/webkit-children.json: no such file or directory` in `split, resize, reload, and WebView churn stay bounded`, in both runs. - [o] F70 — P2: Write each Wails binding failure once and in the error form. Wails writes `10:27AM ERR Binding call failed: Bound method returned an error: …` from its own logger for every binding call that returns an error, in addition to the page's line for the same failure, and Tauri writes no such line; F47 recorded that every Wails error goes through its error handler, which this path does not. Cause, identified on 2026-10-05 in the Wails v3.0.0-beta.27 source: `HTTPTransport.httpError` (`pkg/application/transport_http.go`) logs every error that it returns to the page with `t.logger.Error(err.Error())`, and the same `t.error` also logs the transport's own write failures, which no request receives, so the host cannot tell the two apart without matching message text. The correction belongs to the framework: `httpError` should not log at error level an error that it returns to its caller. That needs a change to Wails (a fork or an upstream change); core uses upstream Wails. Decided on 2026-10-05: fork Wails in the account min-median-max and correct it there. Done on 2026-10-05: the branch `soksak/http-error-log` of `min-median-max/wails` (from v3.0.0-beta.27) removes the log line of `httpError`, so an error returned to the caller is not logged and a failed write of the error response still is; `apps/wailsv3/go.mod` and `packages/host/wailsv3/go.mod` replace `github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3` with that commit. Red: `TestHTTPTransportErrorIsReturnedNotLogged` of the fork failed against v3.0.0-beta.27 with `the returned error was also logged: "... Invalid runtime call: missing object value"`; Green: it and the `pkg/application` tests pass, and core's consumer test `TestTheTransportReturnsAFailedCallWithoutLoggingIt` failed against v3.0.0-beta.27 with `the transport logged the failure it returned` and passes with the fork. Observed on 2026-10-05 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64): `core.plugins.install` of a plugin missing from the registry wrote `ERR Binding call failed: Bound method returned an error: plugin no-such-plugin is not in the registry` in the log of the 0.0.3 Wails release and no such line in the log of the debug build with the fork.

The final full window run of 2026-10-07 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, main display 2560×1440 at scale 1) and the first `repeat` of `resize.test.mjs` `maximising and restoring` on Wails logged `error: verify: 1 fail — V7c 미리 게시한 자리 == 그려진 자리 (최대 0.50px … tab-… drawn 203,33 760×286.5 declared 203,33 760×286 …)`. The card rects of the layout are snapped to device pixels (`onGrid` in `packages/soksak/src/dom.ts`), so at scale 1 a drawn height of 286.5 is half a device pixel that the native surface cannot take. Done on 2026-10-07. Measured: the V7c failure text now names the drawn card, its style, the plane and `devicePixelRatio` (`packages/workbench/verify.js`), and it showed `card style 762px×342.5px · devicePixelRatio 2`; `host.window` reported `scale 2` at 1200×760 for about 1.5 s after the restore that Wails performs with `-[NSWindow zoom:]`, on a screen that `host.screens` reports at scale 1. The view of `packages/soksak/src/dom.ts` read the device pixel ratio twice for one layout: once for the rects that `commit` reports to the host and again when `paint` writes the elements, so the ratio that AppKit changed in between moved the card to 342.5 while the host kept 342. The snapshot now holds one `step` that the commit and its paint both use, and the resolution listener draws again on the new grid. Red: `a paint writes the rects its commit reported when the ratio changes before it draws` (`packages/soksak/test/dom.test.mjs`) failed with `288.5px` against `288px`, and `resize.test.mjs` `maximising and restoring` failed in the first run on Wails four times. - [o] F92 — P1: Find why the drag lag of `outside.test.mjs` `native content, cards, and the sidebar rail stay aligned` exceeds its p90 limit on a 60 Hz display. On 2026-10-07 (macOS 26.6.2 arm64, main display 2560×1440 at 60 Hz and scale 1): the three full window runs of that day and two runs of the check alone failed on both hosts with p90 55.9 to 58.0 ms against the limit of 3 frames (50.0 ms), while the median stayed at 41.0 to 42.6 ms within 2.5 frames; load average 7 to 18 on 11 processors. Each transaction is presented about 30 ms (2 frames) after it begins. The frame limits of [native surfaces](spec/native-surfaces.md) were set on 2026-10-01 before the display changed, and the failure occurs at moderate load in every run, so it is not classified as load until the frames of the late steps are measured. Measured in the same runs: consecutive layout transactions begin about 33 ms (2 frames at 60 Hz) apart, for example #4300 to #4303 at −7.5, +24.4, +57.6 and +91.2 ms, because the page begins the next preparation only after the previous transaction was presented, while `diagnostics.drag` sends a step every 16 ms; the screen therefore shows a new layout every second frame and the frame between them shows the earlier layout one frame longer, which puts the 90th percentile above 3 frames. The [native surfaces](spec/native-surfaces.md) contract states the limits at 60 Hz, so the cadence of the transactions has to fit one frame, or the steps that the screen cannot show have to be measured against the presented layouts; the measurement of a transaction's stages at 60 Hz decides which one. The classification of this check as load in the record of F46 is replaced by this item. Measured on 2026-10-07 with `transactionCadence` (`e2e/drag-measurement.mjs`), which `outside.test.mjs` now prints before it judges the lag: over one drag the transactions began at a median interval of 33.4 ms (Wails, 47 transactions) and 33.3 ms (Tauri, 46), and each took a median 30.6 ms and 30.1 ms from its beginning to its presentation (load average 12). In the page's layout trace the next preparation begins about 1.5 ms after a presentation, so the interval is spent waiting for the animation frame after the preparation and for the presentation of that frame. Because a newer preparation extends the window's open transaction ([native surfaces](spec/native-surfaces.md#placement-sequence)), beginning it before the earlier commit would join both layouts in one commit, so the wait between the presentation and the next animation frame is the part to measure next. The layout trace now records `requested`, the time the page asks the host to wait for the presentation of its drawn DOM (`surfaceLayoutAfterPresentation`; [endpoint](spec/endpoint.md), contract case `diagnostics.capture-stop.payload-preserves-layout-stages`, Red in the Go and Rust cases with the five-stage record, Green after the change; `surface_layout_test` and `window_titlebar_reload_test` read the record with `SURFACE_LAYOUT_TRACE_STAGES`, which also removes their writes past four values). Measured on both hosts at load average 15: from the beginning to the request a median 17.8 ms (p90 18.8), from the request to the presentation 12.7 ms (13.5). The presentation is confirmed at the refresh that shows the drawn frame, so no refresh is lost there; the next preparation begins about 1.5 ms after that confirmation, after the animation frame of that refresh has run, and its draw waits for the following one. A cadence of one frame needs the earlier transaction to commit when WebKit hands the drawn frame's layers to the UI process rather than after the refresh shows it; the WebKit presentation callbacks are to be read next. Read in the WebKit source (main, 2026-10-07): `-[WKWebView _doAfterNextPresentationUpdate:]` calls `WebPageProxy::callAfterNextPresentationUpdate`, which sends `DrawingArea::DispatchAfterEnsuringDrawing` to the WebContent process; `RemoteLayerTreeDrawingArea` adds the reply to the commit bundle of its next rendering update, and `RemoteLayerTreeDrawingAreaProxy::commitLayerTree` runs the reply right after it applies that layer tree, inside the same Core Animation transaction, not when the screen shows the frame. The host registers the wait only when the page reports its draw, after the rendering update that contains the draw has committed, so the reply rides the next rendering update; that is the 12.7 ms from the request to the presentation, and the native commit comes one update after the DOM. Registering the wait before the draw attaches it to the update that runs the draw only if no rendering update runs between the registration and the page's animation frame; a rendering update in between would commit the native layout one frame before its DOM, which the [placement sequence](spec/native-surfaces.md#placement-sequence) forbids, so the correction has to bind the reply to the update that contains the draw. Measured with `native/darwin/tests/presentation_order_test.m` (60 Hz, load average 4): a page posts a script message in the animation frame that draws, and the UI process registers the presentation wait as soon as the message arrives; the confirmation came before the next refresh, that is with the commit of the drawn update, in 26, 24 and 21 of 40 draws in three runs, so the arrival of a script message and the commit of the update that sent it have no fixed order. `RemoteLayerTreeDrawingArea::dispatchAfterEnsuringDrawing` starts a rendering update on a zero-delay timer when the wait arrives, so a wait registered with the preparation, before the page draws, can attach to an update without the draw. With these WebKit interfaces the host cannot bind its commit to the update that contains the draw; the current order (register after the draw, commit with the next update while the open transaction holds the DOM) is the one that keeps the DOM and the native layout together, and at 60 Hz it gives a transaction every second frame. Meeting the 60 Hz limits of the contract therefore needs a decision: change the contract to that cadence, or a different presentation design that WebKit does not offer through these interfaces. Correction and completion on 2026-10-07: the conclusion above that these WebKit interfaces cannot give a transaction every frame at 60 Hz was wrong. The record of G1.4-14-4-2 measured this check at 60 Hz on 2026-10-01 with a median of 20–35 ms and a 90th percentile of 27–45 ms, with native commits 5–8 ms after each step, and that record was not read before the conclusion. The cause is F43 (2026-10-05): `drawPrepared` drew in the next animation frame, which waits for the display refresh, while a draw made outside a rendering update is carried by the rendering update that the host's presentation wait starts at once (`dispatchAfterEnsuringDrawing`); F43 stated that its change added no frame, which missed that update. The page now draws a prepared layout in the next task (`nextTask` in `packages/workbench/layout-queue.js`), which never runs inside a rendering update and its observation round, so the protection of F43 holds ([native surfaces](spec/native-surfaces.md#placement-sequence)); `animationFrame` and its 10-second error are removed ([native host](spec/native-host.md)). Red: `outside.test.mjs` failed on both hosts with a 90th percentile of 56–58 ms and a transaction interval of 33.4 ms, and `a prepared draw runs in the next task, not in the checkpoint that answered its preparation` (`packages/workbench/test/layout-queue.test.mjs`) failed without `nextTask`. Green: the 310 workbench tests pass; after both hosts were rebuilt the check passes 3 of 3 on each host with transactions 16.7 ms apart and 90th percentiles of 36.7–37.5 ms (Wails) and 20.1–20.8 ms (Tauri) at load average 7 to 9 on the 60 Hz display, and `outside.test.mjs`, `files.test.mjs`, `projects.test.mjs` and the padding check of `terminal.test.mjs` pass without a ResizeObserver loop error. `presentation_order_test` remains as the measurement that a script message and its commit have no fixed order.

The criterion of the check was wrong, not the code: the check counts the allocations of the thread that posts the notifications, on which the observers and the records run. Red: `make -C native/darwin repeat TEST=activity_observers_allocation_test COUNT=3` failed with `allocate 201 blocks more ... (2201 against 2000)`. Green: the same target passed 10 consecutive runs, each with `0 blocks more ... (2000 against 2000)`.

A request of 200 to 10000 calls exceeded the 10 second page request timeout while another window covered the check window, because one call then took 1 to 35 ms instead of 0.5 ms, with a load average of 44 to 48 on the machine; the requests of 50 calls ended within 9 seconds. Measured on 2026-10-19 (debug builds of this checkout, macOS, 500 calls in 8 rounds, empty first-run windows): growth per call before the collection 688 B (Wails) and 1102 B (Tauri), after the collection below 20 B in both. Both hosts send a page call through `fetch` to a custom scheme handler (the Wails runtime to `/wails/runtime`, the Tauri IPC script to `ipc://localhost`), so each call allocates a request, a response and JSON strings in both pages.

Done: `make host-calls MINUTES=M` (`--idle-minutes`) waits M minutes without input per round instead of the calls and reports the WebKit malloc growth per minute before and after a collection, with the reclaimable bytes of WebKit malloc. Sources read: the runtime of the Wails fork starts no timer on macOS while idle (the drag environment poll ends after at most 100 polls of 50 ms; the region tracking runs only on Windows), and both hosts send the same host events to the page; the host status `host.log` counts the notices `debug-log-changed`. Measured on 2026-10-19 (debug builds of this checkout, macOS, load average about 20, visible inactive windows, disposable configurations with the same project, two terminal tabs and one browser tab, both measured at the same time, 2 rounds of 3 minutes): growth per minute before the collection 57 KB (Wails) and -76 KB (Tauri); after the last collection both pages read 82 MB footprint and 38 MB WebKit malloc with 6.9 MB and 6.8 MB reclaimable; empty first-run windows grew 55 KB and 27 KB per minute in the second round. `host.log` counted 3 notices in 2 minutes in each host, all from the status reads of the measurement. Decision: the idle page of neither host produces garbage, and with the same state started fresh the difference of F200 (119 MB and 31 MB reclaimable against 86 MB and 0.6 MB) does not appear, so no idle source exists to fix. One structural difference remains for activity: the Wails fork evaluates every host event in every window whether or not the page listens to it (`EventIPCTransport.DispatchWailsEvent`, `WebviewWindow.DispatchWailsEvent`), while Tauri evaluates an event only in webviews with a listener for it (`Listeners::emit_js_filter`); F200.3 measures it.

The count of such events during a session was not measured, because neither host counts the events that reach a page; the idle page received none (idle growth 53 KB per minute after the change against 55 KB per minute in F200.2). Decision: an unlistened event costs the Wails page garbage and retained malloc, so the Wails fork evaluates an event only in a page whose runtime reported a listener for its name: the runtime reports the first listener of a name with `wails:event:listen:<name>` and the removal of the last one with `wails:event:unlisten:<name>`, `wails:runtime:ready` empties the reported names, and an event emitted before the runtime is ready is still kept and flushed. Each request has an id and a promise; a reply resolves or rejects it by id; a cancel sends `{id, cancel: true}` and rejects with reason `cancelled`; the declared timeout (default 10000 ms, integer from 1 to 600000 ms) rejects with -32000 and `command <name> did not reply within <ms>ms`; `peerLost(reason)` rejects every open call with `process-ended`, `surface-closed` or `sidecar-ended`; a reply to an ended call is discarded and reported as a late reply, and the layer remembers the last 256 ended calls. The layer reports `timeout`, `peer-lost` (with reason), `late-reply` and `open-calls` to a `report` function. Result: `packages/plugin-api/snapshots.js` runs over a given `send` and `onMessage` and holds no transport. `createSnapshotSender` (plugin side) keeps at most one snapshot in transit per status; a push during the flight marks the status dirty, the acknowledgement sends the latest value, and each dirty value that a newer value overwrites is reported as skipped. `peerLost(reason)` reports each status whose acknowledgement is pending as stalled, and with reason `surface-closed` it also reports the dirty value as stalled. A process that starts again creates a new sender, so its first push of each status is sent at once. `pull(status)` answers `{seq, value}`. `createSnapshotReceiver` (workbench side) acknowledges each snapshot before it passes the value on, and `pullSnapshots` requests each status once. `snapshotReporter` in `packages/workbench/plugin-processes.js` adds the skipped and stalled counts to `core.plugin.losses`. No timer is used. Split: this item declares no event; `host.trace.declared-ui.snapshot.skipped` and `host.trace.status.stalled` have the host relay as emitter, and F212.3-6 declares them. The views do not connect the channel yet, and no view end calls `peerLost`; the views come in F212.7. A failure of a persistent service is the end of the service process that a revival finds before it spawns, a start failure of the creation path (the ready bound, an exit before the endpoint, the hello bound), or a connection that the reader ends for a protocol violation; a reattach is not a failure, and one disconnect counts at most one failure. A check that changes the frontmost application under such load meets this wait; the stall watch records it with its stacks.

Decision: `sok` is a short-lived process without a writer ([logging](spec/logging.md#entrances)); the failure of any `sok` command is its exit status and its message on the standard error ([cli](spec/cli.md#output-and-exit-status)), which the code already writes for every path, and the audit of the sources of `sok` found no discarded error result. The detached command is the only run whose standard error had no reader. Done: both hosts give the command the standard error of the host, which is `logs/host-<boot>.stderr`, start it before the final flush (`StartAppUpdate`, `start_update`) and store `host.update.start` (`pid`, `command`). The exit status of the detached command has no reader, because the host ends before the command replaces the bundle; a failed command restores and starts the earlier bundle, whose run begins with `log.open`. The alacritty engine applies each OSC 133 mark at its position in the byte stream, moves the cursor to a new line on `A` when it is not at column 0, keeps a prompt or output state, and rejects `redraw` values other than `0`, `1`, and `last`. On a primary-screen resize in the prompt state it reflows, clears the rows from the first row of the cursor's logical line to the bottom, and places the cursor as many rows below that row as it was before the reflow. It clears after the reflow, not before as this item first stated, because the reflowed logical line and cursor exist only after the reflow. The cursor placement is measured: zsh and readline both move up by the cursor row count of the width they last drew at; with the cursor left in place zsh drew one row low, and with the cursor at the first row bash overwrote the output row above the prompt. The sidecar starts zsh with `ZDOTDIR` pointing at an embedded `.zshenv` and bash with an exported `PROMPT_COMMAND` entry that sources an embedded script. Measured bash 3.2 behavior shaped the script: `--posix` does not read `ENV` unless the shell runs as `sh`; a file read by `source` does not see the `DEBUG` trap and a trap it sets is replaced by an earlier one, so the entry records the trap before `source`; `$(builtin trap -p)` does not show the parent's traps; `LINENO` advances on each line of `PROMPT_COMMAND`, so the first attempt reported an empty input line as a command; an entry ending in a newline broke `PROMPT_COMMAND` extended as macOS recommends (`"$PROMPT_COMMAND; x"`); and a `SIGWINCH` during startup made the trap run for a command after the first `A`. Red: the engine tests `a_resize_in_the_prompt_state_clears_the_cursor_logical_line_to_the_bottom`, `redraw_last_places_the_cursor_as_redraw_1_does`, `redraw_last_scrolls_the_screen_when_the_offset_row_is_below_the_bottom`, `prompt_rows_that_the_reflow_moved_into_the_scrollback_are_cleared`, `a_prompt_start_moves_a_cursor_off_column_zero_to_the_next_line`, and `an_unsupported_redraw_value_is_rejected_without_a_state_change` failed first; `tests/shell_test.rs` failed on each bash defect above; `tests/shell_redraw_test.rs` (real zsh and bash with the engine) showed the overwritten row; and the window check failed on both hosts with `START-` shown three times while the first prompt had reported a command start. Green: engine tests 79 of 79, `shell_test.rs` 7 of 7, `shell_redraw_test.rs` 2 of 2, and the sidecar workspace tests pass; on rebuilt Wails and Tauri the window checks `a resize redraws a wrapped zsh input line without rows of the previous width` and the bash case pass with a narrowing, a widening, and a divider drag (three runs per host), `e2e/terminal.test.mjs` and `e2e/terminal-font.test.mjs` pass 62 of 62, and `pnpm test`, `make native-test`, and the structural checks pass. A second size change before the shell redraws can still make the shell draw at a width that is no longer current (measured with bash 3.2 at 30, 45, and 60 columns in the sidecar test); the real-input tier was not run for this change.

      - [o] V5-51-6-1 — P1: Keep the page's cursor state equal to the drawn cursor. On Tauri, after `terminal.focus` the region was the native first responder while `terminal.cursor.focused` stayed false until the next output, and `terminal.cursor.shape` reported the configured policy instead of the shape a program requested with DECSCUSR. Acceptance: the measured cause, a fix, contract and plugin tests, and the window check on both hosts. Done on 2026-09-25. Cause: `present_screen` sent only the raster; the callers that changed the screen through output, scrolling, or input also sent the screen event, but focus, theme, cursor-policy, selection, and configuration redraws did not, so the page kept the previous cursor. A `screen.read` request showed the sidecar already focused. The page also copied only the position, visibility, and focus from the screen cursor. Fix: `present_screen` sends the screen event of every raster it presents, the callers send a screen event themselves only when no image region exists, and `terminal.cursor` reports `drawn` (shape and blink request after the program's request and the focus rule). Red: the contract test `a_focus_change_sends_the_screen_with_the_presentation_that_draws_it` (an idle sidecar answered the focus change without a screen event) and the plugin test `the drawn cursor follows the screen event while the policy shape stays` failed before the change.   - [o] V5-52 — P1: Show the resize and pointer cursors over dividers and icons. On 2026-09-25 hovering a divider or an icon sometimes showed the arrow instead of the drag or pointing-hand cursor. Acceptance: the measured cause, a fix, and a real-input check on both hosts that reads the system cursor over each divider and control after pointer moves, focus changes, and native surface updates. Progress on 2026-09-25: a probe with posted HID moves read `NSCursor.currentSystemCursor` on the rebuilt V5-50 hosts. With the application active, both hosts showed the left-right resize cursor over `core.divider` and the pointing hand over `core.card.close`, also after the pointer had been over a terminal region. With Finder active and the application window frontmost at the point, the icon kept a non-hand cursor. `PageClientImpl::setCursor` in WebKit applies a page cursor only when the view's window is active, `[NSApp _cursorRectCursor]` is nil, the window is frontmost at the pointer, and the hit view is inside the web view. The inactive case follows the first condition. Two conditions can also fail in the active window: the terminal region is an `NSTextView` with an I-beam cursor rectangle, and native surface and document views above the main page can be the hit view. Remaining: reproduce the reported active-window case and identify which condition fails. Done on 2026-09-25. Cause: after a change of the window's view geometry (a divider move, a card resize, a terminal presentation), AppKit sends `cursorUpdate:` to the view under the pointer; `WKWebView` does not handle it, so the message passed through the window composition view to `NSView`, whose tracking-area manager set the arrow, and the page cursor returned only on the next pointer move. Fix: `SPWindowComposition` answers `cursorUpdate:` by hit-testing the current pointer location and passing a mouse move at that location to the tracking owner of the WebKit view under the pointer that tracks mouse moves, which sets the page cursor; it passes nothing while a mouse button is pressed. Red: the real-input check `dividers and card icons show their cursors after moves, focus changes, and terminal output` read `arrow` on both hosts over a divider that the pointer rested on while a card focus change (a click on a card icon) ran. Green on rebuilt Wails and Tauri: the check passed three runs per host, the real-input tier passed 36 of 36, the window checks passed 92 of 92, and `pnpm test`, `make native-test`, and the structural checks pass.

On 2026-09-25 at a load average of 11–15 it passed 5 of 12 runs on both the committed build and the V5-50 build, failing with `red inline image did not reach native pixels: 0` or `same-name replacement did not reach native pixels: 0`. Acceptance: the measured reason the capture shows no image after the display event, a fix, and tracked repeats that pass. Done on 2026-09-25. Measured: in the failing runs the captured terminal held only text (for example `30,30,30×271523 208,208,208×1425`) and no image pixel. Causes: (1) the sidecar placed an image at the cursor it read after the whole output chunk had been fed, so when the image sequence and the following prompt arrived in one chunk (more often under load) the image was anchored at a later row; (2) the page's inline image event was sent before the raster that drew the image. Fixes: the engine attaches the cursor cell and scroll generation where the sequence appears to the event, and the sidecar sends inline image events with the presentation that draws them (after the draw error when drawing fails). Red: the engine test `an_inline_image_is_anchored_at_the_cursor_where_its_sequence_appears` and the contract test `an_inline_image_event_follows_the_presentation_that_draws_the_image` failed before the change, and the window check failed in 6 of 7 runs on one host at load averages of 8–16. Green: the engine and vt-core tests pass, and the window check passed 10 consecutive runs on both rebuilt hosts at load averages of 9–11. The full window run is pending for the final batch.
  - [o] V5-54 — P1: Keep one failed window check from breaking the next Tauri checks. At a load average of about 15 on 2026-09-25, after one terminal check failed on Tauri, the following checks failed at `diagnostics.fixture` with `image "view" has no raster geometry` until the application restarted. Acceptance: the measured state after the first failure, a fix in the application or the fixture, and a tracked run in which a forced first failure leaves the next check passing. Done on 2026-09-25. Measured state: the failing region was placed and shown by its page, had a 0×0 frame and a layer scale of 1 (it never had a size), and its surface had no native frame. Cause: the page draws a new card before the host applies the card's rectangle, so a new terminal page could place a shown image region before any preparation had given its surface a native frame. The host treated that region as an error; the error failed the terminal page's mount, which left the card empty with `image "view" has no raster geometry` in its status row, and the region stayed shown in the host registry, so every later raster refresh, including the one in `diagnostics.fixture`, failed until the application restarted. Green on rebuilt Wails and Tauri: ten consecutive runs passed on both hosts, the window checks passed 165 of 167; two synthetic input cases were refused after AppKit reported a nonzero button mask, then passed when rerun, and `make native-test`, `make boundaries`, `make exposure-check`, `make e2e-check`, and `make docs-check` pass. `pnpm test` failed once in the VT recovery test, recorded as V5-62.

(1) The page rejected every drag point outside the view, so a drag toward the start of a line that crossed the left edge stopped at the last point inside it; a real drag from cell 5 to 20 points left of the view copied `EFTE` instead of `LEFTED`. The page now moves a drag point after the press to the nearest point inside the view. (2) The engine passed each cell's own point to alacritty's `SelectionRange::contains_cell`, whose second argument is the cursor point; alacritty leaves a block cursor at a selection boundary uninverted, so both end cells of every selection were drawn unselected while they were copied (`FT` was shown selected and `EFTE` was pasted). (3) The selection always anchored at the left edge of the pressed cell and ended at the right edge of the pointer cell, so a drag toward earlier cells excluded both end cells; the engine now chooses the edges from the drag direction so that the pressed cell and the pointer cell are both selected. Progress on 2026-09-25. The real-input check `a real wheel over a long history is shown without lag, stalls, or reversal` writes 100,000 lines (the engine keeps its limit of 10,000 lines of history), scrolls with 120 wheel events 16 ms apart while recording, and decodes the top line of every frame from a mark whose column encodes the line number; event and frame times share the mach clock. Measured causes: (1) every output chunk, scroll, and input sent the page a full `screen` event even while the host held the previous raster, and a text screen with every cell field was about 240 KB, so during a 100,000-line output the page processed screens for more than 180 s after the output ended; (2) the renderer created a CoreText line and parsed and allocated two colors for every cell of every frame, about 22 ms for a 122×40 screen. Fixes: the sidecar sends a `screen` event only with a presentation and sends the one current screen after the host answers `consumed`; the page cell carries only `ch`, `width`, `link`, and set attributes; the renderer draws a single glyph of the base font with `CTFontDrawGlyphs` and reuses colors between cells (about 3.7 ms for the same screen). A later Wails run in the full real-input suite measured a 261 ms stall. Sidecar tests, frame tests 17 of 17, terminal plugin 103 of 103, `pnpm test`, `make native-test`, and the structural checks pass. Open: each wheel event is shown about 30 ms after it is posted, about three frames of this display, not the next displayed frame that this item requires; the user has not yet judged the speed. During the full window suites the Tauri host fell into the `no raster geometry` cascade of V5-54, and the committed code without these changes produced the same cascade at the same load (19 of 40 Tauri checks failed); one real-input run on Wails reported that a plain click opened a link, which three reruns did not reproduce. Measured on 2026-09-25 on the bundled builds of c18adb9: at a load average of 2.3 both hosts passed with start lags of 28 ms (Wails) and 30 ms (Tauri), end lags of 17 and 19 ms, longest stalls of 21 and 20 ms, largest steps of 8 lines, and no backward frame; at load averages of 23–49 Wails stalled 142 ms and then moved 55 lines in one frame, which the check, reading line marks modulo 97, counted as one backward frame. Open as before: a wheel event is shown two to four frames after it is posted instead of by the next frame, and the user has not judged the speed. Done on 2026-09-25: the user judged the scrolling speed of the current builds acceptable. The real-input check passes on both hosts with the limits it states (start lag, end lag, and longest stall at most 50 ms, no backward movement, and the display reaching the final viewport); a wheel event is shown two to four frames after it is posted, not by the next frame, because the input passes through WebKit, the page, the host, and the terminal service and the raster is drawn and committed before the display shows it.

On 2026-09-25, during a full window check run at load averages of 5–15, `VT recovery preserves the live service and session across client restart` in `scripts/test/vt-recovery.test.mjs` failed once in `pnpm test` and once in the third of five `make node-repeat` runs with `FAIL retain did not close exactly the orphan session: {"error":"surface actor closed before retain"}` and `sidecar client session failed: Broken pipe`; eight runs on the committed code and eight later runs on the working tree passed. Acceptance: a repeat target that reproduces the failure, the measured cause, a fix, and a repeat run without failures. Done on 2026-09-25. Reproduced with `make node-repeat FILE=scripts/test/vt-recovery.test.mjs NAME="VT recovery preserves the live service" COUNT=20` (failure in run 6 at a load average of 12). Cause: every surface actor of a persistent connection writes through the connection's output sink, which the input loop clears when it reads EOF; when the client's output side closed first, an actor's next write failed and the actor ended, leaving a registry entry whose actor could no longer receive the close that `retain` sends. Fix: a persistent service's sink treats a closed client output as a detach, clears that client, and keeps the actor; the stdio sink still reports the error. Red: the unit test `a_persistent_sink_detaches_when_its_client_output_closed_and_a_direct_sink_fails` did not build before the change. Green: the vt-core tests pass and the same repeat target passed 40 of 40 runs at load averages up to 31.

Cause: `clear` sends `ESC[3J` and then `ESC[2J`; the grid library moved the visible lines into the history on `ESC[2J`, so the lines erased from the screen became history and the scrollbar appeared. Red: the engine tests `erase_display_clears_the_screen_without_moving_it_into_the_history` (history `(0, 3)` instead of `(0, 0)`) and `erase_above_clears_every_line_above_the_cursor_and_the_line_up_to_it` (`one` left on the first line) failed on the previous engine.
