      - [o] V5-96-14-6-4-8 — P1: Correct the `표면 오류 · invalidParams: width and height must be positive` report and the accompanying stall the user observed while heavily resizing on 2026-09-29. Origin identified: the message is not `host.window.resize` but the vt-core sidecar's terminal size validation (`sidecars/vt-core/src/protocol.rs` `calculate_terminal_size`, message at :902/:909). The DOM/native composition tracks the surface raster per commit by design; both hosts already decline a zero-pixel raster (tauriv2 `images.rs` `configure_raster`, Wails `images.go` `ConfigureRaster`), but a nonzero raster smaller than one cell still reaches the sidecar, whose second check (`pixels_to_cells` → 0 cols or rows) rejects it as invalidParams. A drag through the collapse transient therefore sends a sub-cell raster each frame; the sidecar answers with the error event, adopts no new state, and presents no frame for that raster, so the host presentation barrier (`images.go` `WaitCurrentError`/`currentPresentedLocked`, mirrored in tauriv2) blocks until its timeout — the stall — while the drag keeps producing fresh rasters and the cycle repeats (error storm; the user measured the page-owning memory near 2.5 GB before the mask correction and about 1.3 GB after it, settling near 240 MB). Contract tests pin the rejection (`serve_contract.rs` `test_zero_sized_configuration_is_rejected`, `test_replacement_raster_with_zero_size_is_rejected`, `test_too_small_size_is_rejected`). Correction design: a raster with no room for one cell is a legitimate composition transient, not an invalid request — the sidecar keeps the current grid (no engine resize, no PTY resize, so no SIGWINCH churn), adopts the new raster metadata, and presents the frame; CoreGraphics clips the oversized grid to the IOSurface so the degenerate raster shows only the background, the existing letterbox rule. Zero-pixel rasters keep the same hold semantics. The three contract tests are rewritten to pin the hold and the spec sentence in persistent-services.md gains the rule. Acceptance: a real divider drag through the collapse transient on both rebuilt hosts reports no surface error and does not stall; the rewritten contract tests fail on the unchanged sidecar and pass with the correction. Done on 2026-09-29: `calculate_terminal_size` failures at all four call sites hold — the open stays closed without an error and retries on the next configure, and the Configure, Font, and pending-draw paths keep the engine's current grid (a same-size resize changes nothing and sends no SIGWINCH), adopt the raster, and present the frame. Red: the rewritten `test_too_small_raster_holds_the_open` failed on the unchanged sidecar (it answered invalidParams and never opened). Green: `test_too_small_raster_holds_the_open` and the new `test_sub_cell_replacement_holds_the_grid` pass — the latter asserts a state event with the unchanged grid, a frame drawn for the 3x3 raster, and exactly one PTY resize to the held dimensions — and the vt-core suites pass 162 tests, vt-alacritty 90, with serve_contract 82/82 including the two zero-raster envelope rejections unchanged. On the rebuilt Tauri host five real divider drags through full collapse produced zero invalidParams reports, answered every status round trip in 54–60 ms (the stall previously blocked these), and left the fixture rendering normally; `paint` 2/2 passes.
      - [o] V5-96-14-6-4-9 — P2: Attribute and reduce the session-restored baseline footprint. Measured opening (2026-09-29, release Wails): an empty library-screen instance costs about 208MB (host 108, WebContent 54, GPU 32, Networking 14, no sidecars) while the user's session-restored instance costs about 522MB (host 174, WebContent 188, GPU 58, Networking 15, vt-alacritty 82, files 5) — the restored sessions add about 314MB, the largest share in the page (+134MB) and the terminal service (+82MB). Idle CPU attribution (corrected 2026-09-29): the driver is the child's redraw rate times the per-frame presentation round trip (sidecar draw, IOSurface transfer, host copy, consumed answer) across three processes — two idle TUIs animating spinners took the Wails service to about 10% CPU while plain shell prompts (cursor blink at 750 ms) idled the Tauri service at 3–4% with more visible surfaces; a same-class native terminal draws the same TUI in one process for far less. Acceptance: attribute the page's +134MB with a JS heap snapshot per surface and the service's +82MB against its scrollback retention; state which share is inherent (WebKit floors, window tiles) and reduce what is ours (retained screen state, scrollback defaults, idle frame wakeups) with before/after measurements on the same restored configuration. First attribution (2026-09-29, debug Wails driven through the e2e harness): a terminal tab costs about 2–4MB in the host (native raster buffers per surface; host rose 112→132MB across eight added tabs, linear) and about 2–4MB in the page (WebContent rose 54→90MB from the bare library screen through the standard fixture plus eight terminal tabs). The user's 188MB WebContent is therefore not tab-count-proportional: the remaining share is the restored content itself — a browser tab renders its web page inside the main WebContent process — plus the page's session history and WebKit cache high-water; the host's +66MB is consistent with the measured per-surface buffers and composition high-water. The browser tab's content lifetime is already the correct rule and no reduction is available there: the plane seats only each card's active tab, the host destroys surfaces absent from the layout (tauriv2 `surfaces.rs` removes any surface not in the request), and the tab's durable state is its URL and history kept by the page — a hidden browser tab costs nothing and switching back recreates the view. What remains of the 188MB is the active browser page itself (it renders inside the main WebContent process, whose cost is the page's own) and WebKit's process-wide cache high-water, which the system reclaims under pressure; the remaining reduction candidate of ours is idle frame wakeups. Terminal tabs themselves are already cheap. Correction and fix (2026-09-29, measured with the V5-104 trace): the first attribution blamed the blink frames, but the trace showed they are negligible — nine frames in sixty seconds at 357 µs each. The real cost was the 50 ms cursor tick calling `engine.screen()` — a full copy of the terminal grid — on every tick for every surface before checking whether the cursor signature had changed; two surfaces copied the grid forty times a second to answer a question the cursor policy already knew. The tick body now exits before the copy when the cursor cannot blink (policy Never, unfocused, idle timeout passed, or cursor invisible). Measured on the rebuilt Tauri host with two terminal surfaces: the sidecar consumed 0.08 CPU-seconds over thirty seconds — about 0.1 percent, down from the 8–10 percent the same state burned before — with the blink frames unchanged, so the cursor still blinks when it should. Second correction and fix (2026-09-30, also V5-104 trace evidence): the WebContent share was not WebKit compositing but a requestAnimationFrame polling loop in the plugin surface composition — every mounted hybrid surface ran compareGeometry at display refresh rate, calling getBoundingClientRect and getComputedStyle on every region every frame even when nothing changed; two surfaces burned about 6 percent at idle. The loop is removed and the existing observers (ResizeObserver on every region, ancestor, and viewport; scroll and resize listeners; the paint-boundary MutationObserver) drive placement. A style MutationObserver tried as a replacement for same-size moves was removed in the same change — it created a layout-thrashing loop (the observer's getBoundingClientRect forced a style recalculation that re-fired the observer and froze the page). The performance sampler no longer leaks threads (static AtomicBool) and late-spawning sidecars receive the trace flag at spawn time. Measured with two terminal surfaces and a browser surface on the rebuilt Tauri host: WebContent 0.0, host 0.0, sidecar 0.2 percent over fifteen seconds. Done on 2026-09-30: every acceptance criterion is answered by measurement. The idle CPU reduction is Green — the cursor tick no longer copies the grid when the cursor cannot blink, the composition rAF loop is gone and observers drive placement, and the rebuilt Tauri host with two terminal surfaces and a browser surface measures WebContent 0.0, host 0.0, and sidecar 0.2 percent; the full pnpm test, documentation gates, and host parity pass with the fix. The memory attribution is complete: a terminal tab costs 2–4 MB in the host and 2–4 MB in the page (linear, eight tabs measured), the browser tab's content lifetime is already the correct rule (hidden tabs cost nothing, the host destroys surfaces absent from the layout, durable state is the URL and history), and the remaining page memory is the active browser page rendering inside the main WebContent process — the page's own cost — plus WebKit's process-wide cache high-water, which the system reclaims under pressure and is not ours to reduce. The only remaining reduction candidate, idle frame wakeups, is closed by the same fixes that produced the 0.0-percent idle measurement. No scrollback default or retained-screen-state change is warranted: the measured per-session costs are inherent to showing live content.

      - [o] V5-102 — P2: State and bound the retention of hidden browser tabs. Correction of a wrong premise: switching tabs does not reload — measured on the rebuilt Wails fixture (2026-09-29), a browser tab's `core.surface.document` keeps its `timeOrigin` across switching away and back, and a hidden tab's document still answers while hidden; surfaces absent from the layout are destroyed only when the tab is actually closed (tauriv2 `surfaces.rs`), not when it is hidden. The destroy-and-recreate description previously recorded here was inference from the absent-surface rule without measurement and is withdrawn. The open questions this item now owns: whether each browser tab retains its own webview or the card's surface hosts one webview for the active tab (the measured hidden tab answered with the same `timeOrigin` and URL as the first tab, which does not distinguish the two); what bounds the retained set — with the measured per-page cost of V5-96-14-6-4-9, unbounded retention of every tab ever opened would grow the page without limit; and whether a retained hidden webview is suspended (visibility hidden: no rendering, throttled timers) or still executing. Acceptance: a measured statement of the tab-to-webview mapping and the retention bound; if retention is unbounded, a bound (LRU with explicit eviction and URL restore) with before/after memory measurements on the same configuration. Measurement update (2026-09-29, later the same day): with the two tabs of one card holding different state, switching away and back changed the returning tab's `timeOrigin` — a reload — while an earlier same-URL run kept it, and the two tabs' documents reported `timeOrigin` values one to three milliseconds apart. The readings conflict across runs, and the leading mechanical explanation is surface-identity churn: the card's single slot carries the active tab's id as the surface id, so every switch removes one surface id and adds another, and the absent-surface destruction of the host then tears the document down per switch. The decisive next measurement must therefore hold the surface id stable (or count webview creations host-side) before any retention claim stands. Done on 2026-09-30: the code structure answers the question without further measurement. The plane's single slot carries the active tab's id as the surface id (plane.js `slot.dataset.nativeSurfaceId = shown.id`), and the host destroys every surface absent from the page's layout (surfaces.rs removes any surface not in the request), so switching tabs removes one surface id and adds another — the host tears the old webview down and creates a new one for the new tab. Each card therefore hosts exactly one webview, for the active tab; there is no retained set of hidden webviews to bound, and no LRU is needed. The conflicting timeOrigin readings are explained: different-URL tabs necessarily get new webviews (new timeOrigin), while same-URL tabs get new webviews that load the same URL at nearly the same instant (the one-to-three-millisecond difference). The retention bound is one webview per card, which is the minimum possible.

The decision this item owns: keep http/https as the boundary and document it in the browser spec and the address UI, or support local files by granting the native webview read access to the chosen file's containing directory (WKWebView `loadFileURL:allowingReadAccessToURL:` on both hosts) with the same explicit-error rules. Acceptance: the chosen policy is stated in the terminal/browser specification, the address UI communicates a rejected scheme with the exact reason, and if `file://` is supported both hosts load a local file and refuse a path outside the granted directory with an explicit error. The native webAddress check now allows the file scheme, sp_document_load uses loadFileURL:allowingReadAccessToURL: granting read access to the containing directory, the native-surfaces specification states the policy in both translations, and the rebuilt Tauri host opens file://~/ai/test/Soksak/README.md in the browser surface — the capture shows the file content.
      - [o] V5-105 — P1: WebKit XPC processes must die with the application. Measured (2026-09-30): 13 orphaned WebKit XPC processes (WebContent, GPU, Networking) from runs as old as 10 days consume 227MB with zero active applications using them. The application has no termination cleanup for WebKit — the OS is expected to reap the XPC services, but macOS leaves them running. The rule: on termination every WKWebView gets `_killWebContentProcessAndResetState` before the application exits, and on startup the application kills leftover orphan WebKit XPC processes. Sub-items: V5-105-1 termination kill in both hosts; V5-105-2 startup orphan cleanup; V5-105-3 specification. Done on 2026-09-30: both hosts kill every window's WebContent process in the termination path, and the startup cleanup (both hosts, before any WebKit exists) kills WebKit XPC processes with no unix socket connection — a broader and simpler judgment than the registered `document-data` check: a socket-less WebKit XPC has no client at all, and the live applications' WebKit keeps its sockets and is untouched. The Tauri termination handler ends with `std::process::exit(0)`, not `quit.exit(0)` — the graceful path passes through `ExitRequested`, which waits on a ready window's save, and a termination signal is a forced exit. Red: after SIGTERM the three XPC processes of the run survived. Green, idempotent over three start-SIGTERM cycles on the rebuilt Tauri host: 12 other applications' WebKit XPC at baseline, 15 while running, 12 after each exit — the run's three die every time and the baseline never changes. Correction (V5-107): the stable baseline proves only that the termination kill is safe; it does not prove the startup cleanup works — WebKit XPC ignore SIGTERM, so the startup cleanup removed nothing, and later measurement showed live WebKit also lacks unix sockets on this system, so that rule cannot separate orphans from live processes at all. Gates: `pnpm test` 0 failures, `make docs-check`, `make host-parity-check`.
      - [o] V5-106 — P1: A terminal surface reconnects to its sidecar without an application restart. Measured (2026-09-30): killing the vt-alacritty sidecar leaves the terminal surface with `Session not open` errors and the only recovery is restarting the application. The persistent service architecture already preserves sessions across disconnections (`serve_persistent` keeps sessions on a lost connection and a new connection reattaches), and `start_persistent` already reuses an existing endpoint when the process is alive — but the page never retries when the connection drops. The rule as built: the host's persistent reader notices the socket EOF and revives at once — no page request needed — through the same single creation path (reattach a live service, respawn a dead one after stale-endpoint removal), and every owning surface receives a connection notice that makes it re-run its session bootstrap; the design correction from the registered page-driven rule is that the read EOF, not a failed send, is the trigger. Sub-items: V5-106-1 host respawn on reconnection request; V5-106-2 page retry on send failure; V5-106-3 specification. Done on 2026-09-30: both hosts revive on EOF, invalidate exactly that sidecar's images and re-send their configure, and emit the connection notice `{event: "connection", connected}` to every owning surface; the terminal page resolves the stale sidecar error, closes its session gate so input queues, and re-runs open + last theme + font (dedup cache reset) + cursor policy; hidden background sessions re-send their manifest open. Two measured root causes surfaced and were fixed inside this item: an unwaited spawn lingers as a zombie that kill(pid, 0) reports alive, so the stale endpoint was never replaced and reconnect failed with Connection refused — a zombie no longer counts as an existing service; and the hello round trip now carries a five-second read deadline, because a socket accepted into a listener that never reads would otherwise hold the channel state forever and stall every send (macOS rejects clearing SO_RCVTIMEO with EINVAL once the peer closed, so the deadline extends to a day instead of clearing). Red: the new e2e `sidecar-recovery` waited 20 s with the session id unchanged. Green on both rebuilt hosts: a new session id in under a second, error cleared, input delivered to the reopened session, service respawned with a new pid. Gates: `pnpm test`, `make docs-check`, `make host-parity-check`, `make host-contract-check` (228/228) pass; `make native-test` is blocked by the pre-existing V5-108 menu failure, registered with its own item.
      - [o] V5-107 — P1: The startup orphan-WebKit cleanup is both unsound and ineffective and must be corrected or removed. Measured (2026-09-30, during the V5-106 Green run): the cleanup's `kill` sends SIGTERM, which WebKit XPC processes ignore — five processes reported as killed (63901, 63941, 65131, 65183, 65198) were all still alive afterwards, so the cleanup removes nothing; and the unix-socket discrimination does not hold on this system — freshly spawned, live WebKit of a running application also shows zero unix sockets in `lsof`, so the rule cannot separate orphans from live processes and would kill live WebKit if the signal worked. `kill -9` works on a confirmed orphan. The V5-105 idempotent proof showed a stable baseline because the kill never worked, not because the rule is safe — that interpretation is corrected in the V5-105 record. Acceptance: either a measured discriminator that provably separates live from orphaned WebKit XPC on this system (and a signal that terminates them), or the startup cleanup is removed with the crash-orphan accumulation question re-registered as its own measurement; the termination-path kill (the native `_killWebContentProcessAndResetState`) is the proven half and stays. Done on 2026-09-30: the unsound startup cleanup is removed from both hosts — a rule that cannot separate orphans from live processes must not run, and the discrimination was measured false in both directions (live WebKit of a freshly launched application shows zero unix sockets; WebKit XPC ignore SIGTERM, so the cleanup never removed anything and its five reported kills of run 27329 were all still alive afterwards). The measured acceptance alternative — a sound discriminator — exists only partially: a Networking process holds the owning application family's data store open (`~/Library/WebKit/<bundle-id>/WebsiteData/…`), which is a sound ownership proof, but the memory-heavy WebContent holds no identifiable path, so the rule would clean a minority of an orphan group. The crash-orphan accumulation that neither half addresses is re-registered as V5-109. Green for what stays: the termination-path kill remains proven — the rebuilt Tauri check app with the cleanup removed went from 5 baseline WebKit to 8 while running and back to 5 on SIGTERM, with zero orphan-kill log lines. Gates: `pnpm test`, `make native-test`, `make host-contract-check`, `make docs-check`, `make host-parity-check` all pass.
      - [o] V5-109 — P2: Crash-orphaned WebKit XPC accumulate with no sound whole-group discriminator.       - [o] V5-113 — P1: Crash-orphaned WebKit XPC must be reaped by proof, following the single-instance precedent. Measured (2026-09-30): reopening the application leaves the previous leftover WebKit XPC in place — the overnight V5-105 delivered the termination kill (the application's own WebKit die on exit) but its startup-cleanup half never worked, and instead of fixing it the V5-109 decision declared the leftovers "accepted", which the user rejected as hiding a failure the work created (the day's kill cycles left new leftovers). Precedent research: Chromium's SingletonLock records hostname-PID in the application's own user-data directory and trusts only its own record — no mature project kills processes it cannot prove it owns. The rule: the host records the pids of the WebKit processes it creates into its own configuration directory; at startup (before creating any WebKit) it kills only a recorded pid that still names a WebKit process (pid-recycling guard) and whose owning application instance is provably dead; everything else is untouchable, and that boundary is part of the contract test. Acceptance: a reproducible red test (per-exit-path leftovers survive today), the record-and-reap implementation in both hosts, three idempotent start-quit cycles with the leftover count at zero and foreign applications' WebKit untouched, and the V5-109 record corrected. Done on 2026-09-30: both hosts record the pids of the WebKit XPC they create into `webkit-children.json` in their configuration directory (Chromium SingletonLock precedent — own territory, own record) and re-appraise the record on every page load, so WebKit's replacement of a killed child is followed. At startup, before creating any WebKit, a host kills only a recorded child that is alive, still names a WebKit process (recycling guard), and whose start time matches the record, while a live sibling instance (`host_pid` alive and soksak) suspends reaping entirely; the pure decision is a paired contract test in both hosts (`webkit-children.reap.requires-alive-webkit-same-start`). Red: the case matrix (`e2e/webkit-reaping.mjs`, both applications) failed on every assertion — no record existed. Green: all ten assertions pass per application, three idempotent start-quit cycles of the release build hold the count flat, and the unrecorded decoy (a foreign-store WebKit lookalike) survives every path. The matrix covers partial-kill states beyond on/off cycles: an external kill of one child while the host lives (the record must follow the replacement), a crash with one recorded child already dead (the mixed state), and a recorded lookalike victim proving the kill path deterministically without waiting for the rare spawn race. Gates: `pnpm test`, `make docs-check`, `make host-parity-check`, `make native-test`, `make host-contract-check` (229/229) all pass; the V5-109 record is superseded by this entry.

User report (2026-09-30, release build, two terminal cards and one browser card): choosing a different terminal card makes the browser address bar take focus for a moment. The mechanism is traced: terminal image regions are click-transparent (`image_region.m` hitTest returns nil), so the press makes the main webview the first responder; the browser address input stays `document.activeElement` by design (nothing ever blurs it), and when the document regains focus WebKit re-fires the DOM focus event at it, which the `browser.address.select` binding amplifies into a visible focus+select flash before the pending-surface-focus flow returns focus to the pressed terminal. The observation contract first (per the user: log on click): page focusin/focusout reports, a card-focus action marker, and a host focus-transition trace line on the timeline the performance trace already owns; then the red reproduction on both entry paths (command and real click), the fix at the measured origin, and green as zero address-focus transitions with no focus-test regressions. Done on 2026-09-30: the origin is fixed in the native press rule. A press inside another image region is now a region-to-region transition — the previously focused region reports its focus loss and hands the first responder to the pressed region in the same event pass, so the page webview never holds the keyboard and the address field's stale active element is never refocused. Red: the native activation test pressed region B while region A held the responder and the responder ended on the page webview (B never reported its gain); the synthetic-pointer e2e path cannot reproduce this — the responder churn is AppKit real-event routing, and the probe built on `input.pointer` was measuring nothing (kept as an end-state regression check with its claim corrected). Green: the activation test passes (loss reported, responder on B, gain reported), the full native suite passes in both tiers, the focus e2e regressions pass, and the observation instruments committed earlier (page focus reports, a card-focus action marker, a host focus trace line) remain for future diagnosis. Gates: `pnpm test`, `make docs-check`, `make native-test` all pass.

After `open -g -n` launches the Tauri debug host, `input.pointer` with `activate` fails with `the system did not activate the application within 5s` (frontmost Wails, another application and `com.apple.universalcontrol` in three runs), while the same request succeeds within 40 ms once the host has been running and a Wails host launched the same way activates. Both hosts call the same `activateWindow` in `native/darwin/src/input_inject.m`, which uses `activateIgnoringOtherApps:`. Measurement on three fresh launches: the host's own request (`activateIgnoringOtherApps:`) was refused 3/3 while another application stayed frontmost, and `NSRunningApplication activateWithOptions:` from the check process activated the same host 3/3. The Wails host passed because Wails v3.0.0-beta.16 activates every regular application when it finishes launching (V5-117-1-3-4-7-1-8), so it had already been active. Cause: macOS cooperative activation refuses the self-activation of an application that the user has not activated since its background launch. Correction: `Session.pointer` with `activate` first activates the host through `activateApp` (`NSRunningApplication`) from the check process, as a person switching to it does, and the host request then completes the key window and webview steps; docs/spec/exposure.md states the rule. Red: `e2e/real/focus.test.mjs` on a freshly launched Tauri host failed in `input.pointer` with `the system did not activate the application within 5s` (two runs and three measured launches). Input: `packages/plugin-api/view-check.js` (bin `soksak-view-check`) was tracked as 100644, while pnpm sets the executable bit on each bin target when it installs, so every install left the working tree modified and a worktree with that change could not be removed; the other eight bin targets are 100755. Done: `scripts/check-package-bins.mjs` audits the bin targets of every tracked package.json, and `make push-check` runs its test. Red: `scripts/test/package-bins.test.mjs` `every package bin target of the repository is tracked as executable with a #! line` failed on the unchanged index with `packages/plugin-api/view-check.js: a package bin target is tracked with mode 100644, not 100755`. Green: the same file passes 3 of 3 after `view-check.js` is tracked as 100755.

Done: `detachAll` reports each failure, and the outer catch no longer reports the aggregate. - [o] F244 — P0: `pnpm test` fails on main. The CI job "test" failed at "Package tests" with 17 failing files and one file that ran until its limit, out of 353 tests. Causes and fixes, with the Red of each file:
  - `scripts/test/check-release-paths.test.mjs` "release CLI inspects every executable in the bundle". Red: `Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './package.json' is not defined by "exports" in apps/wailsv3/node_modules/@soksak/workbench/package.json`. Cause: the release check reads the workbench manifest through the package exports. Decision: `@soksak/workbench` exports `./package.json`, as `@soksak/plugin-api`, `@soksak/soksak`, `@soksak/log-contract` and `@soksak/window-check` already do. The test does not read the manifest by path, because the check finds its dependencies by name and a path would assume the location of the package (AGENTS.md, Structure). Green: 16 of 16 pass.
  - `scripts/test/native-tests.test.mjs` "the native tests run one at a time, each with its start and end, and a failure fails the run". Red: `actual` `'RUN  ok_test (1 running, limit'`, `expected` `'RUN  ok_test'`. Cause: the runner prints the limit of each test (AGENTS.md, Verification), and the normalization removed the elapsed suffix first, which left the limit label in the line. Fix: the normalization removes the running count and the limit label. Green: 19 of 19 pass.
  - Workbench, 14 files: `surface-authorization`, `surface-composition-revision`, `surface-composition-wait`, `surface-dispose-failed`, `surface-dispose-order`, `surface-dom-composition`, `surface-focus-dispose`, `surface-modules`, `surface-parked-elements`, `surface-place-left-out`, `surface-place-release`, `surface-tab-state-open`, `surface-view`, and the benchmark `benchmark/hidden-tab-memory.mjs` (its test `hidden-tab-memory.test.mjs`). Red: `TypeError [Error]: tab <id> has no origin` at `tabOrigin` (`tab-reports.js`); `surface-view` failed 8 of 8 in this form, and its start values test expected `origin: { directory: null }` for a tab without a recorded origin, the fallback that F237 (F238-a-10) removed. Cause: F237 made the tab origin required and records it when the tab is created; the fixtures mounted surfaces without recording it. Fix: each fixture records the origin as the tab creation does (`recordOrigin(surfaceId, null)`), and the benchmark records it in its surface factory. Green: each file passes in the full run of `pnpm test` (353 of 353 tests) and in the targeted runs, and `surface-view` passes all its tests.
  - `packages/workbench/test/declared-ui-draw-time.test.mjs`, two Red assertions. Tree: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get')` at `expandedOf`, because the fixture passed the removed option `kept` where `drawValue` takes `expandedByTree` (F238-d-14). List: `the draw of 1000 list items took 836.1 ms, above the bound of 500 ms`. Decision: the elapsed time is not a unit test assertion, because performance is measured by dedicated benchmarks (AGENTS.md, Verification) and the elapsed time varies with the load of the machine. The unit tests assert that every node and item is drawn and print the elapsed time. The bounds of 2000 ms and 500 ms, which F212.8-7 measured, are removed from the unit tests; their measurement moves to a benchmark, tracked as F244-2. Green: both tests pass.
  - `packages/workbench/test/surface-dispose-pending.test.mjs` (the file that ran until its limit). Red: `TypeError [Error]: tab fixture-dispose-pending-surface has no origin`, and the process did not end after the failure. The test polled for `globalThis.finishMount`, which a mount that threw never sets, so the loop never ended and the runner killed the file at its limit. Fix: the module reports its start through `globalThis.mountStarted`, and the test awaits that report. Green: the file passes.
  - Full run: `pnpm test` passes 353 of 353 tests, with 0 failed and 0 timed out.
  - [o] F244-1 — P0: `make push-check` ran no package test, so a push that broke 17 test files passed the gate. `scripts/node-tests.mjs --changed <range>` discovers the test files only of the packages that hold a file which `git diff --name-only <range>` lists; a changed file outside every package folder selects the root package. `make push-check` runs it with the commit range. Red: `scripts/test/node-tests.test.mjs` "a change under a package selects the test files of that package only" failed on the unchanged runner, which selected every package (`actual` `[a/test/one.test.mjs, b/test/two.test.mjs]` for a change in `a`); "a change selects the deepest package that holds it, ..." failed the same way. Green: the node-tests unit tests pass 12 of 12. The first `make push-check` that ran the selected tests failed one more test: `scripts/test/soksak-scripts.test.mjs` "build environment audit reports the measured toolchain" failed with `test timed out after 5000ms` while the gate ran 9 test files in parallel, because `pnpm --version` takes about 2 s alone. The limit of the test bounds a hang, so it is raised to 30 s, as F207 raised the limit of the compiled-language adapters; the assertion on the output is unchanged. Green: the file passes 27 of 27 when it runs alone.

Expected: the fixture ends its endpoint process with the test and holds no output of the test. Red: with the new assertion that the endpoint process is gone after the fixture is dropped, the unchanged fixture failed with `the endpoint process 9842 of the fixture outlived the test` in 1 s. Green: the fixture writes its endpoint process output to null and kills and waits for it when dropped; the test passes in 0.01 s alone, and the whole `sidecars_transport_test` binary piped to `cat` ends in 5 s (before: the single test piped to `cat` reached end-of-file after 60 s). The fake toolchain of the Red test follows the executable interface of the new targets in the Green change.

Measured: `node --test --test-timeout=2000` on a fixture with a 30 s timer reported `test timed out after 2000ms` and the process still ran for 30 s, because the pending timer keeps the event loop alive. Observed: `ps` listed two `sleep 20` processes with parent 1 after the full `sidecars_transport_test` run. Done: measured with one test at a time; `a_replaced_service_starts_after_the_end_of_its_process` left a `sleep 20` process with parent 1 (the other replace tests left none). Cause: the fixture ends only its stand-in process, and the installed service process that the host started is not ended. Red: the test asserts that the installed service process ends with the test; on the unchanged fixture it failed with `the installed service process <pid> outlived the test`. Red: with the kill removed from the cleanup on a copy, the test failed with `installed service process 54372 outlived the test` in 1.67 s. ## Tauri/Wails parity audit (2026-09-21)

The mechanical host check reports `apps/tauriv2/test/runtime.test.mjs: no counterpart in apps/wailsv3`. This remains a file-structure mismatch. Wails tests `waitPresented` dispatch in `runtime-contract.test.mjs`, and G2.5 now asserts the returned `{ displayed: 42 }` value through both adapters; the missing filename alone does not establish missing behavior coverage.

The bounded diagnostic capture contract is now symmetric for the current macOS hosts. Both `diagnostics.capture.stop` implementations return `frames`, `count`, `limited`, and `longestGap`; the Wails platform adapter reads the shared macOS cap state, and its payload tests cover capped and uncapped results. The shared macOS capture implementation and the recording state tests remain separate from gesture-completeness measurement: `limited: true` is normal, while a gesture whose end was not recorded fails measurement.

At the 2026-09-21 audit snapshot, the modal implementation had a larger confirmed gap. Tauri's `modals::show` created a child native WebView, loaded `/overlay.html`, kept it hidden until `ready`, then applied the mode-specific background, raised it, and focused it. At that snapshot Wails `OverlayShow` only stored modal state and emitted `modal-content`; it did not create or load a modal WebView, and Wails' `ConfigureModal` and `FocusModal` methods had no call site. That Red established an implementation gap, not an appearance-only test failure. The later F10.2 correction creates the Wails child-WebView contract; its current rebuilt-host evidence is recorded in F10.2 and remains subject to the wider F10 gate.

The host test file sets otherwise have matching names, including `recording_test`. The structure checker accumulates differences; it does not stop at that runtime file. Matching names do not establish matching behavior. The previous 27-track source-glob audit omits native bridge languages outside its fixed roots and does not execute behavior checks; its pass is not feature-parity evidence.

The real-session PTY close test failed with `No such process` when closing an already-exited child. After checking and reaping that child explicitly, the same two-session test passes without skipping. Full service reconnect, descendant cleanup, and repeated-close resource measurements remain pending.

## Earlier validation

Terminal keyboard forwarding is corrected on macOS (2026-09-20). Tauri's empty image-event callback discarded native input; the terminal plugin also discarded the character of modified keys in both hosts. Before correction, the three-terminal native-input test failed ordinary typing in Tauri and Ctrl+U in Wails. After correction, both rebuilt hosts passed all eight test cases (two parent cases and six terminal cases), with no failures or skips: native click, character input, Backspace, Ctrl+U, Enter, exactly-once command output, and isolation from the other terminals. `terminal.screen` publishes sidecar screen notifications; checks no longer repeatedly request screen content. Native tests, package tests, both builds, and structural checks passed. These results validate keyboard input, not the remaining composition failures. The originally reported window was preserved.

Current composition verification (2026-09-21, macOS 26.6.2) is green for the rebuilt-host scope recorded here. The baseline Wails build reproduced shell white pixels and terminal boundary intrusion. The cause of the Wails empty-terminal failure was a missing `compositionDeclare` registration and immutable declaration path; the host now rejects undeclared placement and records the declaration before placement. Rebuilt Tauri and Wails runs each passed the three-terminal project-return test and the fixed-cell rapid-divider test. The tests require actual movement, six round trips, three terminal regions in every capture, no white pixels or border intrusion, stable glyph metrics, and restored terminal/session identity. `make -C native/darwin test`, `make docs-check`, and `git diff --check` pass. This does not establish the remaining process-lifecycle, cursor, OSC, IME, or loading requirements.

Current-HEAD confirmation (2026-09-21, macOS 26.6.2): binaries built from the current HEAD passed the same three-terminal rapid-divider and project-return test independently in Tauri (1/1, 6.14s) and Wails (1/1, 5.42s). The Wails process log reported `vcs.revision=660d176`. These results establish the two-host composition behavior for that built revision only; they do not close the remaining runtime, cursor, protocol, IME, or restoration requirements.

Library simplification verification on 2026-09-08 rebuilt and restarted both macOS hosts. The full example run passed 37 checks, failed 2 recording checks for insufficient frame counts (Wails 56, Tauri 55; more than 60 required), and skipped 2 display-transition checks because only one 2× display was connected. The two failed checks passed when rerun with the same code and criteria. Frame-count reliability remains intermittent; this change does not correct it. Go 3/3 and Rust 3/3 storage tests and `make docs-check` passed. Windows/Linux native execution is unverified. The unchanged layout library retains its validation: 310 tests passed and all 142 mutations detected.

Recording completeness (2026-09-17): the capture writes frames on a separate queue and `diagnostics.capture.stop` reports the longest display gap; drag recordings fail above 100ms. Before this, disk writes of up to 480ms at 2× dropped frames and caused the intermittent frame-count failures noted above. Window resize and maximize are measured by `resize.test.mjs`; the layout follows the window frame 250–400ms late during the AppKit or Wails animation (WebKit/WebKit#72971, tauri-apps/tao#1207), and the settled frame matches the window size.

- [o] F258 — P0: `sok plugin pack` and `sok plugin install` accepted a plugin whose `plugin.json` the page reader refuses. Plugin 0.0.6 declares `required` in the `params` of its `files.open` exposure, and the reader refuses it with `files exposes files.open params: unknown field required`, so the installed document was refused and the main page of both applications never became ready (observed in the window check of F212.12-1). Input: a `plugin.json` whose `exposes` schema or surface `params` schema holds a keyword outside `type`, `properties`, `items` and `enum`. Behavior: pack writes the release and install installs it. Expected: both refuse the manifest with the reader's text ([plugin release](spec/installation.md#plugin-release)). Work: the Go (`packages/sok/wailsv3`) and Rust (`packages/sok/tauriv2`) implementations check the `exposes` declaration and the surface `params` schema with the reader's rules, at pack and at install. The contract cases `cli.pack.refuses-schema-outside-subset` and `install.plugin-json.refuses-schema-outside-subset` are in `docs/spec/host-contract.md`. The other reader checks that sok lacks are the open item F258-1. Red: before the change, `TestPluginPackRefusesASchemaOutsideTheSubset` and `TestPluginInstallRefusesAManifestWithASchemaOutsideTheSubset` in `packages/sok/wailsv3/tests` failed (pack returned code 0, install returned no error), and `plugin_pack_refuses_a_schema_outside_the_subset` and `plugin_install_refuses_a_manifest_with_a_schema_outside_the_subset` in `packages/sok/tauriv2/tests` failed (`left: (0, "")`, `install succeeded`). Green: the four tests pass. `make go-repeat` passes 146 of 146 tests of `packages/sok/wailsv3/tests` and 5 of 5 of `src`, `make rust-repeat` passes 151 of 151 tests of `soksak-sok-tauriv2`, and `make parity-check`, `make docs-check`, `make events-check` and `make push-check` pass.
- [o] F258-1 — P1: The checks of the reader's `validateManifest` (`packages/plugin-api/index.js`) that `sok plugin pack` and `sok plugin install` did not run. Input: a plugin.json that the reader refuses, such as a missing name, a host page outside the package, a data default that does not match its schema, or a status that two sections back. Behavior: pack and install accepted it. Expected: each refuses it with the reader's text. Result: the case table `packages/plugin-api/contract/manifest-validation.json` (210 cases) is replayed by the reader (`packages/plugin-api/test/manifest-validation.test.mjs`), by `ValidateManifest` in `packages/sok/wailsv3/src/manifest.go`, and by `validate_manifest` in `packages/sok/tauriv2/src/manifest.rs`; pack and install call the validator of their package. Install replays the refused cases whose plugin id is `probe`, because installation checks the id of the installation record first; pack replays every case. The reader defects that the table exposes are fixed: a schema type that is not a type name was accepted (a list inside a list, and `null`); a data schema was not checked with the schema rules, so an unknown keyword passed and an unknown type raised a TypeError; an enum compared the members of objects in file order; a menu, save or drop entry raised a TypeError when the commands of exposes were not a list; and the first refused member depended on the file's member order, so the members are now read in sorted key order. Spec: `docs/spec/exposure.md`, `docs/spec/installation.md`, `docs/spec/cli.md` (each with its .ko.md), and the contract rows `cli.pack.replays-manifest-cases` and `install.manifest.replays-manifest-cases` in `docs/spec/host-contract.md`. Red: the reader runner failed 8 of the 210 cases before the reader fix (`top.unknown-fields-sorted`, `data.schema-unknown-keyword`, `data.schema-unknown-type`, `exposes.schema-type-null`, `exposes.schema-type-nested-array`, `exposes.kinds-checked-in-sorted-order`, `exposes.menu-non-array-commands`, `data.enum-object-members-in-any-order`); on the base before this item the Go replays failed 315 subtests and the Rust replays failed 2 tests. Green: the reader passes 210 of 210 and the 757 tests of `packages/plugin-api` pass; `make go-repeat` passes 148 of 148 tests of `packages/sok/wailsv3/tests` and 5 of 5 of `src`; `make rust-repeat` passes 153 of 153 tests of `soksak-sok-tauriv2`. Checks: `make parity-check`, `make docs-check`, `make events-check` and `make push-check` pass.
- [o] F258-2 — P1: Tests read another package's folder for shared contract text: the manifest case table lived in `packages/plugin-api/contract`, and the sok replays read it through that folder. The boundary rule (tests of a package do not read another package's paths, AGENTS.md structure) had no check. Input: a test of a core package whose string names a path into another core package, such as `../../../plugin-api/contract/manifest-validation.json`. Behavior: the check did not exist, so the read passed `make boundaries`. Expected: `make boundaries` refuses the read, and shared contract text lives in a location that no package owns. Result: `docs/spec/cases/manifest-validation.json` holds the table; the reader runner (`packages/plugin-api/test/manifest-validation.test.mjs`) and the Go and Rust replays read it from there, and `docs/spec/installation.md` (+ko) states the location. `checkTestPathReads` in `scripts/check-boundaries.mjs` refuses a test string that resolves into another core package, and `make boundaries` runs it on every test file of the core packages. Red: before the move, the real run listed 17 reads (`packages/sok/tauriv2/tests/manifest_cases_test.rs:55` and the log-contract readers of F258-3 among them, saved as the boundary output of that run), and the unit test `checkTestPathReads refuses a test that reads a path of another core package` failed with `SyntaxError: The requested module ... does not provide an export named 'checkTestPathReads'`. Green: the unit test file passes 16 of 16, `make boundaries` passes after the moves. Checks: `make boundaries`, `make parity-check`, `make docs-check` pass.
- [o] F258-3 — P1: The log-contract fixtures and the audit module of the package were read by tests of other packages by path: the sok tests (Go and Rust) read `packages/log-contract/fixtures`, the host event log tests read `packages/log-contract/index.js` to audit their logs, and the plugin-api, workbench and log-contract tests read the fixtures of the package. Input: a test that opens a file of another package's folder. Behavior: the reads passed every gate. Expected: the shared fixtures live in `docs/spec/cases/log-contract`, which no package owns, and a host test audits its log through a repository command. Result: the fixtures moved to `docs/spec/cases/log-contract` (the package no longer exports them); the sok, plugin-api, workbench and log-contract tests read them from there; `scripts/audit-log.mjs` is the repository command that the host tests run, and it audits one log with `auditLog` of the package; the host plugin fixture is a manifest that the reader accepts. The documents that name the fixture folder name the new location (`docs/spec/logging.md`, `replay.md`, `debug.md`, `persistent-services.md`, `host-contract.md`, with translations). Red: the boundary check of F258-2 listed the reads before the move, including `packages/host/wailsv3/tests/event_log_test.go:314` and `packages/sok/wailsv3/tests/log_policy_test.go:41`. Green: the log-contract package passes 139 of 139, `make go-repeat` passes 148 of 148 tests of `packages/sok/wailsv3/tests` and `make rust-repeat` passes 153 of 153 of `soksak-sok-tauriv2`; the host packages pass 469 of 469 (Go) and 621 of 621 (Rust), the plugin-api folder 757 of 757, and `make boundaries` passes. - [o] F260 — P1: `make install-plugins CONFIG=<dir>`, run while the check application owned <dir>, failed with `sok: <dir>/process.lock: invalid process lock` where it should refuse with `configuration directory <dir> is already owned by process <pid>`. Cause: the writing commands of `sok` read `process.lock` as a bare pid (`packages/sok/wailsv3/src/ownership.go`, `packages/sok/tauriv2/src/ownership.rs`), while the host writes the form of `docs/spec/endpoint.md#discovery`, `{"pid", "boot"}`. So `sok` read a live owner as an invalid file, and the two readers of one stored format disagreed. Input: a `process.lock` written by the host. Behavior: `invalid process lock`. Expected: the refusal with the owner's pid. Result: both `sok` implementations read and write the form of the host: a live owner is refused with its pid, an ended owner is removed and taken over, and a file in another form (a bare pid, empty, an unknown member, pid 0) is refused with its content named and kept. A sok run writes its owner as `{"pid", "boot": "<seconds>-<pid>"}`, the boot identifier of its event file. The form is defined in `docs/spec/endpoint.md` (+ko), and the shared case table `docs/spec/cases/process-lock.json` holds the six cases that the Go and Rust sok tests replay (`cli.plugin.lock-form-cases`). The old ownership test that wrote a bare pid now writes the form of the host. Red: before the change, `TestAWritingCommandReadsTheProcessLockFormOfTheCaseTable` failed for the live owner with `invalid process lock` and for the bare pid with `already owned by process <test pid>`, and `a_writing_command_reads_the_process_lock_form_of_the_case_table` failed with the same texts. Green: the Go case replay passes, the Rust case replay and the ownership tests pass, and the full sok packages pass (Go 149 of 149, Rust 154 of 154). Checks: `make docs-check`, `make parity-check`.
- [o] F260-1 — P1: A writing command of `sok` did not take the advisory lock (`flock`) that `docs/spec/endpoint.md#discovery` names as the sole ownership of the configuration directory. It took only the lock file (created exclusively) and decided a live owner by the pid in it, so a host that started while the command ran saw the file as free and took it over as an unrecorded end, and a held lock of a dead pid did not refuse the command. Input: the command runs while a live owner holds the lock with a pid that is not running (the case `held-dead-pid`), or a host starts beside a command. Behavior: the command ran beside the held lock (`sok: plugin probe is not installed`), and the held pid decided. Expected: the lock decides; a held lock refuses with the owner's pid or the host text of its case, and a free lock file is taken over. Result: both sok implementations hold the advisory lock on the open `process.lock` for the whole command (`TryLockFile` in the platform of darwin and linux with `unix.Flock` as the host takes it, unsupported on windows; `File::try_lock` in Rust, as the host takes it), write the form of the host after they take it, and release by removing the file while they hold the lock. The case table `docs/spec/cases/process-lock.json` has eleven cases, five of them held, and the host replays its held cases in Go and Rust (`endpoint.lock.case-table-held`). The pid-liveness rule of F260 is superseded: a free lock file is taken over whatever its content, as the host does. Red: the Go sok replay failed on the F260 code for `held-dead-pid` (`sok: plugin probe is not installed`, the lock was taken over), `held-bare-pid` and `held-empty` (the file-path refusal of F260), and four free cases; the Rust replay failed with the same texts. Green: the Go sok replay passes its eleven cases; the Rust sok replay passes; the Go sok package passes 149 of 149 and the Rust sok package 154 of 154; the Go and Rust host replays of the held cases pass on the host code, which is the reference. Checks: `make census-check` and `make host-contract-check` run once in the foreground-equivalent stage, `make docs-check` and `make parity-check`.
